title: On R-Matrix Formulation of qq-Characters
abstractText: Abstract We introduce an R -matrix formulation of qq -characters and corresponding Frenkel–Reshetikhin deformed W -algebras. The R -matrix featuring in the construction is of Ding–Iohara–Miki (DIM) algebra, while the type of the qq -character is determined by the network of Fock representations corresponding to a web of 5-branes geometrically engineering a quiver gauge theory.Our formulation gives a unified description of qq -characters of $$A_n$$ A n type and their elliptic uplifts.

title: Organelle distribution and protein translation defects in radial glia cells with mutations in Eml1
abstractText: Abstract Cerebral cortical development is a finely regulated process, depending on key neuronal progenitors, giving rise to post-mitotic neurons that migrate to superficial regions in the developing brain. Disruptions can give rise to severe cortical malformations that are associated with intellectual disability and intractable epilepsy. Mutations in EML1/Eml1 , coding for a microtubule (MT)-associated protein, lead to subcortical heterotopia (SH) in both humans and mice. In developing mutant mouse brains, ectopic apical radial glia (aRG) progenitors were found outside the normal proliferative ventricular zone (VZ). The normal role of Eml1 in these cells remains to be precisely determined. Using proteomics and imaging approaches, we compared brain tissue from control and mutant mice and identified microtubule and organelle dysregulation. Eml1 influences the trafficking of organelles to different compartments of aRG, where they may be involved in local functions. Thus, we find that mitochondrial and polysome distribution are altered in mutant conditions. Indeed, Eml1 interacts with translational machinery, and an overall downregulation of translation is observed when analysing the translatome of Eml1 mutant aRG. Paradoxically, an upregulation of translation-related mRNAs is also observed. These new data uncover an unprecedented function of Eml1, as well as associating novel subcellular patho-mechanisms with severe heterotopia formation.

Mapping Aluminum Flows in the United States Using Advanced Bayesian Material Flow Analysis
abstractText: Abstract This paper presents a Bayesian material flow analysis (MFA) of aluminum in the U.S. economy, reconciling a 2017 baseline and updating the system through 2022. We introduce ARCADE (Abiotic Resource Cycles, Allocations, and Dynamics in the Economy), a unified Bayesian MFA framework integrating system definition, data pedigree, and probabilistic reconciliation under physical constraints. ARCADE combines government statistics, trade records, and industry reports into a physically consistent network and reports uncertainty-aware metrics. Results show continued U.S. reliance on imports of unwrought and finished aluminum products. The posterior median end-of-life (EOL) collection rate was 66.8% [57.2%, 79.9%] in 2017 and 67.6% [62.3%, 73.9%] in 2022. Median domestic retention of collected EOL scrap was lower in 2022 (52.7% [49.6%, 55.6%]) than in 2017 (56.4% [51.7%, 60.5%]), although the credible interval for the change spanned zero. Across robustness cases varying source weighting, pedigree-to-uncertainty mappings, and prior strength, domestic retention remained below 60%. Spatial analysis identified mismatches between EOL scrap generation and domestic remelting capacity. These findings show that improved collection alone may not increase domestic recycling when processing constraints persist. We observe a continued import dependence, efficient circulation of prompt fabrication scrap, and limited domestic retention of collected EOL scrap.

title: Nash equilibria as limits of approximate equilibria of finite games
abstractText: Abstract We study finite-player normal-form games with compact metric action spaces and bounded Borel measurable payoffs, which need not be continuous. Our main theorem shows that every Nash equilibrium of such a game can be recovered as the limit, in the product weak topology, of $$\varepsilon _n$$ ε n -Nash equilibria of finite restrictions of the game, where $$\varepsilon _n\downarrow 0$$ ε n ↓ 0 and each restriction discretizes the action spaces without changing payoffs. For each player, the finite action sets become dense in the original action space, and the approximating sequence may depend on the prescribed equilibrium. The proof samples from the prescribed equilibrium and uses concentration inequalities to select a realization that approximates it while nearly satisfying all players’ incentive constraints simultaneously. A uniformly vanishing payoff perturbation also makes the constructed profiles exact Nash equilibria of nearby finite games. We provide an example of a continuous game showing that exact equilibria of the unperturbed finite restrictions need not suffice: the game has a Nash equilibrium that is not the limit of Nash equilibria along any sequence of such restrictions.

title: Comparative prognostic performance of FIB-4, AIP, and TyG for all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in FLI-defined MASLD: a nationally representative NHANES 2011–2018 cohort study
abstractText: Abstract Background Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is driven by both fibrosis and cardiometabolic dysfunction, but the relative prognostic value of fibrosis- and metabolism-related indices for near-term mortality remains uncertain. Aim To compare the associations and discriminatory performance of the fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4), atherogenic index of plasma (AIP), and triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index for all-cause mortality (ACM) and cardiovascular mortality (CVDM) in adults with FLI-defined MASLD. Methods This prospective cohort analysis included 4,037 adults with FLI-defined MASLD from NHANES 2011–2018. Mortality was ascertained through linkage to the National Death Index through December 31, 2019. Survey-weighted Cox models, restricted cubic splines, and 5-year time-dependent ROC analyses were used to evaluate associations and discrimination. Age-stratified analyses were performed because age is a component of FIB-4. Results During a median follow-up of approximately 4.5 years, 222 all-cause deaths and 66 cardiovascular deaths occurred. In fully adjusted age-stratified models, each 1-SD increase in FIB-4 was associated with higher ACM risk in participants aged < 65 years (HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.09–1.41) and ≥ 65 years (HR 1.34, 95% CI 1.20–1.50). FIB-4 was also associated with CVDM among participants aged ≥ 65 years (HR 1.37, 95% CI 1.19–1.59), whereas AIP and TyG were not significantly associated with CVDM in this age stratum. As standalone markers, FIB-4 showed higher 5-year discrimination than AIP and TyG for ACM (AUC 0.763 vs. 0.494 and 0.522) and CVDM (AUC 0.785 vs. 0.505 and 0.557). In sensitivity analyses using US-FLI-defined MASLD, the association of FIB-4 with ACM remained significant, and additional adjustment for lipid- and glucose-lowering medications did not materially alter the primary estimates. Conclusions In adults with FLI-defined MASLD, FIB-4 showed stronger near-term mortality risk stratification than AIP and TyG as standalone markers. The cardiovascular findings should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of events and their sensitivity to the operational MASLD definition.

title: First principles study of hydrogen trapping by mono vacancies in ruthenium
Functional and Density-Driven Errors in Density Functional Theory: Quantum Monte Carlo Benchmarks for Solids
abstractText: Abstract We introduce a systematic analysis of density functional approximation errors in solids by separating functional-driven from density-driven contributions using quantum Monte Carlo densities of silicon, sodium chloride, and copper as reference. Typically, functional errors dominate, but we identify important exceptions where the xc component of the density-driven error exceeds the functional error, notably for SOGGA11 in the semiconductor and the insulator. Material dependence is striking: 61% of functionals show error cancellation in silicon versus 16% in copper, and only five functionals surpass LDA accuracy for metallic copper even with exact densities. For silicon and sodium chloride, GILL or BECKE exchange combined with PBE, PW91, or P86 correlation achieves near-exact xc energies on QMC densities, while copper requires specialized functionals like PBEsol or PBELYP. High-quality densities consistently reduce density-driven errors across all systems. Historical analysis reveals that 1990s GGA functionals outperform many modern meta-GGAs, contradicting expectations of systematic improvement along Jacob’s ladder. These results provide practical guidance for functional selection and highlight implications for machine learning potential development, where material-dependent error cancellation may compromise transferability.

title: Serum trace element profiles and gallbladder cancer risk in an Indian population: evidence from a case–control study
abstractText: Abstract Gallbladder cancer (GBC), a rare yet aggressive biliary tract malignancy, varies by geographic location, with greater incidence in the north and northeast of India along the Gangetic belt, suggesting that environmental risk factors may contribute to disease etiology. A total of 912 GBC cases and 1140 visitor controls were enrolled at Tata Memorial Centre, India. The concentration of non-essential (Cr, Ni, As, Cd, Pb, U) and essential metals (Mn, Cu, Se) were measured using the inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometer (ICPMS). Individual metal effects were presented using logistic regression model adjusting for confounders, while joint metal mixture effects were obtained using weighted quantile sum and quantile g-computation methods. A strong J-shaped non-linear association for Cu (OR = 10.21; p-value ≤ 0.005) and Cd (OR = 4.79; p-value ≤ 0.005) was observed. The strongest inter-metal correlation was observed for Mn-U. Exposure to metal mixture showed one-unit increase in the WQS index with increased GBC risk (OR = 6.19; p-value < 0.00001), with the highest weight contributed by Cu (~ 60%), followed by Cd (~ 27%) and Mn (~ 13%). Metal mixtures play a significant carcinogenic role in the development of GBC. Identification of the source of exposure, particularly in the high-risk areas of the GBC, would be useful in primary prevention.

title: Crop Load Management of Plums Using 1-Aminocyclopropane Carboxylic Acid (1-ACC)
abstractText: Excessive fruit set in European (Prunus domestica L.) and Japanese (Prunus salicina L.) plum trees necessitates thinning to optimize crop load, enhance fruit quality, and reduce manual hand thinning. This study evaluated the efficacy of the ethylene precursor 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylic acid (1-ACC) as a chemical thinning agent for the European plum cultivar ‘Vibrant’ and the Japanese plum cultivar ‘Early Golden’. Treatments were applied at full bloom (FB) and at the fruitlet stage (8-10 mm diameter) using 1-ACC concentrations of 150, 300, and 450 mg·L⁻¹. Horticultural measurements included crop load, yield, fruit size distribution, fruit quality, phytotoxic effects, and crop value. Applications of 1-ACC effectively reduced crop load, with FB applications producing greater thinning responses than fruitlet-stage applications. Increasing application rates resulted in decreased yield and crop value, while average fruit weight increased. No hand thinning was required in both years of the study due to poor pollination in the ‘Early Golden’ orchard and atypical fruit drop unrelated to 1-ACC treatments following early fruit development in the ‘Vibrant’ orchard; therefore, commercial thinning was not required. Thinning responses varied by cultivar and application timing, underscoring the importance of cultivar-specific thinning strategies. Ethylene evolution following 1-ACC application supported its role in fruit abscission, with ethylene peaks observed within 24 h and differing in intensity by application timing. These results indicate that 1-ACC is a viable chemical thinning agent for plums, although optimization of application timing and concentration, particularly in seasons with heavier fruit set, is required to balance thinning efficacy with economic returns.

Novel paper-based electrochemical system for detection of anti-spike protein antibodies from SARS-CoV-2
abstractText: Abstract A novel disposable paper-based electrochemical biosensor for detecting anti-spike protein antibodies is presented, featuring the innovative use of carbon dots derived from a biological source and a liposome–biorecognition element complex. The optimized electrochemical sensing platform is described and characterized, regarding its structural and functional properties. The sensor showed a linear response between 0.0010 and 10 µg mL − 1 , demonstrating high sensitivity and a low limit of detection (LOD) of 1.78 pg mL − 1 , as well as good selectivity. Real nasopharyngeal swab samples were tested for the first time using this type of paper-based electrochemical system for anti-spike antibody detection. This approach was designed to mimic the virus's response while ensuring greater sensitivity and selectivity. Overall, a new electrochemical method for screening anti-spike antibodies was developed to monitor vulnerable populations for new SARS-CoV-2 infections and track the development of adaptive immunity within communities, contributing to the development of future point-of-care (POC) analysis without the need for specialized personnel or laboratory facilities.

title: Design and calibration of a division-of-pupil snapshot polarization imaging system
Political stance detection on X during the 2024 U.S. election: a comparative study of classical, neural, and transformer models
abstractText: Abstract As online social networks (OSNs) play an increasingly influential role in political communication, accurately detecting political stance from noisy, short-form content remains a significant challenge in computational social science (CSS). This paper presents a controlled comparison of text classification models for political stance detection during the 2024 U.S. presidential election, focusing on candidate affiliation toward Donald Trump and Joe Biden–Kamala Harris. Using nearly 100,000 posts from X, we define candidate affiliation as a three-class target variable (Trump, Biden–Kamala, or Neutral) and use topic modeling to support keyword development and thematic characterization. Under a unified preprocessing, labeling, and evaluation pipeline, we compare classical machine learning models, sentence-embedding-based neural architectures, and a domain-adapted transformer. Results suggest that task-aligned text representation accounts for most of the predictive signal in this setting. While fine-tuned BERTweet achieves the strongest in-domain performance, carefully engineered classical models, particularly linear support vector machines, remain highly competitive. Multi-feature and ablation analyses further indicate that expanded metadata did not yield reliable gains beyond strong text representations. Overall, this work provides a controlled comparison of text models for candidate affiliation on a heuristically labeled corpus.

title: PPanGGOLiN V2: technical enhancement and extended functionalities for prokaryotic pangenome analysis
abstractText: The exponential growth of genomic data, particularly for microbes, has made pangenomic approaches a gold standard for large-scale comparative genomics. By capturing the full genomic diversity of a species rather than relying on a single reference, pangenomics has transformed microbial genomics, revealing the adaptive potential of bacteria and the evolutionary dynamics underlying functional diversity. Among available tools, PPanGGOLiN distinguishes itself through its graph-based model coupled with statistical gene partitioning. Here we present PPanGGOLiN v2, which introduces substantial improvements across three dimensions: new analytical features that expand what users can investigate, a comprehensive software architecture redesign that improves maintainability and extensibility, and performance improvements that address the computational demands of ever-growing genomic datasets.

title: Natural and anthropogenic factors associated with agricultural productivity in selected Sub-Saharan African countries: The role of water resources
abstractText: This study examines the impact of selected natural and anthropogenic factors on agricultural productivity in 19 Sub-Saharan African countries over the period 1990–2020, using panel data from the FAOSTAT database. Agricultural productivity is measured as kilocalories produced per hectare of agricultural land. The explanatory variables include fertilizer use, agricultural water withdrawal, water stress, population, and agricultural land per capita. The Hausman test supports a fixed-effects specification, which is therefore used in the analysis. The results indicate that population has a positive and statistically significant effect on agricultural productivity, while agricultural land per capita is negatively associated with productivity. Fertilizer use and agricultural water withdrawal are not statistically significant, while water stress shows a positive association with agricultural productivity. The findings suggest that the interaction of demographic pressure, land availability, and water-related constraints shapes agricultural productivity in selected Sub-Saharan African countries. The study highlights the need for improved water resource management, efficient land use, and sustainable agricultural intensification, alongside better-targeted use of production inputs, to support sustainable productivity growth and strengthen food security in Sub-Saharan Africa.

title: A wood-based substrate for passive humidity buffering and visual humidity indication in museum display cases
abstractText: Abstract Eco-friendly substrates combining passive humidity regulation with visual indication remain limited for enclosed museum display cases. Poplar wood was modified by low-temperature ultrasonic co-impregnation with glycerol and anthocyanin. Substrate screening, single-factor tests, and orthogonal experiments quantified the effects of additive dosage and impregnation time on weight percent gain, dimensional stability, and humidity-responsive color change. SEM and FTIR indicated that modification was governed mainly by pore filling and intermolecular hydrogen bonding. The optimal process was 22 wt% glycerol, 0.6 wt% anthocyanin, and 9 h impregnation, yielding a 51% higher 24 h moisture uptake than untreated poplar, with effective pore filling and uniform pigment dispersion. The color response remained detectable after 30 wet-dry cycles. This work provides an environmentally compatible dual-functional wood substrate and a technical reference for passive humidity-buffering and visual monitoring in enclosed exhibition spaces, providing an effective tool for the preventive conservation of wooden heritage artifacts.

title: Polaris: A toolkit for standardized construction, integration, and quantitative testing in Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae
abstractText: Existing synthetic biology toolkits have expanded part libraries and assembly capabilities. However, new users may still encounter ambiguity in construct definitions, hierarchical transitions, genomic integration routes, and quantitative testing procedures. Here, we present Polaris, a Golden Gate toolkit for Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Polaris defines a shared three-level hierarchy. Level 1 stores reusable parts, Level 2 generates transcription units and other intermediate constructs, and Level 3 supports multigene assembly and switching between testing and integration backbones. The toolkit distinguishes part interfaces from transcription unit interfaces, uses BpiI and BsaI in successive assembly stages, and provides parallel ccdB and mScarletI3 screening options. Integration modules and quantitative characterization frameworks were implemented in both hosts and demonstrated using representative genetic parts and activation and repression systems. A companion digital platform further encodes the Level 1 to Level 3 rules for assembly planning. Polaris connects hierarchical construction, stable genetic implementation, and quantitative testing within a common execution framework, providing a practical basis for data accumulation, part standardization, and future automation.

title: Chemical characterization, antibacterial activity, in vitro cytotoxicity, and selectivity of the lipid extract from Sargassum filipendula against multidrug-resistant bacteria
abstractText: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance in multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria necessitates new therapeutic alternatives, and marine macroalgae represent an underexplored source of bioactive lipids. This study characterized the lipid extract (LE) of Sargassum filipendula and evaluated its antibacterial and cytotoxic profiles against MDR hospital isolates. LE composition was determined by GC-MS, and its thermal behavior by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). Antibacterial activity was evaluated using the broth microdilution method (CLSI M07) against Acinetobacter baumannii , Escherichia coli , Klebsiella pneumoniae , Pseudomonas aeruginosa , Staphylococcus aureus , and coagulase-negative staphylococci, followed by determination of the minimum bactericidal concentration. Cytotoxicity was assessed in L929 and MDBK cell lines using MTT, Neutral Red, and Lactate Dehydrogenase assays; Hemolytic activity was evaluated using erythrocytes; and selectivity indices (SI) were calculated for each bacterial species. Palmitic acid (61.07%) and oleic acid (15.90%) were the predominant fatty acids. TGA revealed a total mass loss of 82% across two decomposition stages (296°C, 445°C), and DSC detected no phase transitions, indicating the absence of amorphous or crystalline domains. The LE exhibited bacteriostatic activity against all isolates, with MIC values ranging from 1.18 mg/mL ( S. aureus ) to 2.5 mg/mL ( P. aeruginosa ). Cytotoxicity assays yielded IC 50 values ranging from 0.16 to 1.25 mg/mL, and the hemolytic IC 50 was 12.81 mg/mL. However, the SI values remained below the safety threshold for all tested species (1.45–3.90). The S. filipendula LE is a candidate source of antibacterial compounds against MDR bacteria, although purification processes and in vivo validation are required to establish its therapeutic potential.

title: Intraoperative technology in skull base and vascular neurosurgery: a two-stage cross-sectional national survey
abstractText: Abstract Skull base and vascular neurosurgery rely on diverse intraoperative technologies, but contemporary data describing how frequently they are used at the level of individual operations are limited. On behalf of the Society of British Neurological Surgeons (SBNS) MedTech Committee, we aimed to establish a dated descriptive baseline of reported technology use across three operative paradigms. We conducted a two-stage cross-sectional survey of neurosurgeons in the UK and Ireland via the Society of British Neurological Surgeons (SBNS). Six MedTech Committee members compiled a pragmatic technology list. Respondents reported frequency of use for three exemplar procedures: transsphenoidal pituitary adenoma, retrosigmoid vestibular schwannoma, and pterional aneurysm surgery. Use was recorded on a four-point ordinal scale and analysed descriptively, with Kendall’s tau-b used to explore the relationship between experience and reported use. Twenty-four responses from 20 of the 32 adult or mixed adult-paediatric UK units were analysed (11 units per index procedure). Reported use was strongly procedure specific. Neuronavigation was used always or almost always by 8/12 transsphenoidal respondents but infrequently elsewhere. Endoscopy had displaced microscopy in transsphenoidal surgery, whereas microscopy was used always or almost always by all retrosigmoid and pterional respondents. Indocyanine green and micro-Doppler were routine for aneurysms. Neurophysiological monitoring was universal for vestibular schwannoma but evenly divided for aneurysms. Exoscopes, intraoperative MRI and robotics were used infrequently or not at all; augmented reality was reported by 5/13 pterional respondents. No association was found between experience and reported use, though this was underpowered. Reported intraoperative technology use is strongly shaped by operative paradigm, with established technologies clustering around recurring procedural needs. Newer technologies were used infrequently. Because availability was not recorded, non-use cannot be distinguished from lack of access. These data provide a dated baseline against which future change can be assessed.

IDDA-Scored Abatacept-to-HSCT Course in Pediatric LRBA Deficiency
abstractText: Abstract LRBA deficiency is a rare inborn error of immunity in which impaired CTLA-4 recycling causes immune dysregulation; haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is curative, but no standardised measure of pre-transplant disease activity exists and the role of abatacept as a bridge to HSCT remains ill-defined. We report a 4-year-old girl with compound heterozygous LRBA variants in whom abatacept, given as a planned bridge to transplantation, reduced disease activity within four months (Immune Deficiency and Dysregulation Activity [IDDA] score 54.5 to 22.6), maintained control until transplant, and was followed by an IDDA of 1.0 at 22 months after fully matched unrelated-donor HSCT. Retrospective IDDA scoring was feasible in 32 of 46 published LRBA HSCT patients (22 with and 10 without pre-HSCT abatacept; baseline scores 11.1 vs 11.5), with descriptively higher survival in abatacept-bridged patients (95.8% vs 86.4%; P = 0.34). The IDDA provides a practical metric to quantify disease activity and to evaluate the contribution of pre-HSCT abatacept in LRBA deficiency.

title: Pendampingan Perancangan Sistem Informasi Persuratan Desa Sumberejo Menggunakan Metode Rapid Application Development
abstractText: Pelayanan administrasi surat-menyurat di Desa Sumberejo, Kecamatan Way Jepara, Kabupaten Lampung Timur sebelumnya masih dilakukan secara manual menggunakan arsip fisik, dengan rata-rata 3 hingga 5 permohonan per hari. Kondisi tersebut menimbulkan sejumlah kendala operasional, seperti proses pelayanan yang lambat, kesulitan pencarian dokumen, risiko kerusakan atau kehilangan arsip, serta keterlambatan persetujuan akibat ketergantungan pada kehadiran fisik Kepala Desa. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan mendampingi perangkat Desa Sumberejo dalam proses perencanaan kebutuhan dan perancangan sistem informasi pelayanan surat-menyurat berbasis web menggunakan metode Rapid Application Development (RAD). Metode pelaksanaan dibagi menjadi tiga tahap, yaitu pra pelaksanaan, pelaksanaan, dan evaluasi. Pada tahap pelaksanaan diterapkan pendekatan RAD melalui tahapan requirements planning dan design workshop secara iteratif yang melibatkan langsung perangkat desa sebagai mitra. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan bahwa tim berhasil mengidentifikasi 8 kebutuhan fungsional sistem, menghasilkan rancangan use case diagram, 7 activity diagram, Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD) dengan 19 entitas, serta 9 rancangan antarmuka low-fidelity untuk tampilan desktop dan mobile. Proses iterasi desain dilaksanakan sebanyak 3 kali bersama mitra hingga rancangan dinyatakan sesuai kebutuhan. Kegiatan ini memberikan kontribusi nyata dalam mempercepat digitalisasi administrasi desa dan menghasilkan fondasi perancangan sistem yang siap dikembangkan lebih lanjut.

title: Analisis Keunggulan Komparatif Ekspor Bahan Bakar Mineral Indonesia ke China Tahun 2018-2025
abstractText: This study aims to analyze the comparative advantage of Indonesian mineral fuel exports to China during the period 2018–2025. Mineral fuels are one of Indonesia's important export commodities and contribute to its international trade relations, particularly with China as one of its major trading partners. This study employs a quantitative descriptive approach using secondary data obtained from Trade Map, covering Indonesia's mineral fuel exports to China, China's mineral fuel imports from the world, and Indonesia's total exports. The data are analyzed using the Revealed Comparative Advantage (RCA) method to identify the comparative advantage of Indonesian mineral fuel exports in the Chinese market. The results show that the value of Indonesian mineral fuel exports to China experienced fluctuations throughout the observation period. Export values increased significantly in 2021 and reached their highest level in 2022, before declining from 2023 to 2025. Furthermore, the RCA values recorded in the dataset remained below 1 throughout the period, ranging from 0.19 to 0.33. These findings indicate that Indonesian mineral fuel exports have not demonstrated a comparative advantage in the Chinese market during the period studied. Therefore, improvements in export competitiveness and market positioning are necessary to strengthen Indonesia's presence in China's mineral fuel market.

title: Mekanisme Artificial Intelligence sebagai Mediator Komunikasi Digital dalam Pengayaan Mufradat Bahasa Arab: Perspektif Konseptual
abstractText: Penguasaan mufradat menentukan kemampuan mahasiswa memahami dan memakai bahasa Arab, tetapi pembelajarannya masih bertumpu pada hafalan yang minim konteks dan lingkungan berbahasa yang terbatas. Artikel ini bertujuan menyusun kerangka konseptual tentang cara kerja artificial intelligence sebagai mediator komunikasi digital dalam pengayaan mufradat bahasa Arab. Kata mediator dibedakan menjadi arti teknis dan pedagogis. Metodenya kajian pustaka kualitatif terhadap 25 sumber dalam dua kelompok, yaitu pemanfaatan artificial intelligence dan chatbot dalam pembelajaran bahasa, serta problematika pembelajaran mufradat, dengan sintesis tematik berlandaskan teori mediasi sosiokultural. Hasilnya berupa mekanisme dua lapis. Lapis teknis mencakup pembacaan maksud pengguna, pengelolaan dialog, dan penyusunan jawaban. Lapis pedagogis mencakup input kontekstual, umpan balik langsung, latihan berulang, suasana tanpa penilaian, dan penarikan bantuan bertahap, dengan guru yang memeriksa jawaban. Batasnya meliputi penilaian pelafalan yang lemah, jawaban yang kadang keliru, dan risiko ketergantungan. Pengajar dapat memakai kerangka ini untuk memutuskan bagian latihan mufradat yang diserahkan kepada artificial intelligence dan bagian yang tetap dipegang manusia. Bukti empiris tentang mufradat bahasa Arab pada pustaka yang ditelaah masih terbatas, sehingga kerangka ini perlu diuji.

title: Efektivitas Pelatihan Lubang Resapan Biopori dalam Meningkatkan Kesadaran Pengelolaan Sampah Organik di Desa Sekaralas Ngawi
abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan pelaksanaan pelatihan biopori dan menganalisis efektivitasnya dalam meningkatkan kesadaran masyarakat mengenai pengelolaan limbah organik di Desa Sekaralas, Kecamatan Widodaren, Kabupaten Ngawi. Penelitian ini mengaplikasikan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan metode pengumpulan data meliputi wawancara mendalam, observasi, dan dokumentasi terhadap 15 informan yang dipilih secara tujuan penelitian. Temuan penelitian mengindikasikan bahwa pelatihan yang berfokus pada praktik langsung dapat meningkatkan pemahaman masyarakat tentang fungsi biopori sebagai alat untuk pengelolaan sampah organik dan pemeliharaan air. Selain itu, terdapat perubahan sikap dan perilaku masyarakat yang terlihat dari menurunnya kebiasaan membakar sampah organik, meningkatnya kesadaran mengenai kebersihan lingkungan, serta mulai dilakukannya pemilahan sampah dan pembuatan lubang biopori di area rumah tangga. Keberhasilan pelatihan didorong oleh semangat masyarakat, bantuan pemerintah desa, keikutsertaan tokoh masyarakat, dan penggunaan metode pelatihan yang partisipatif. Namun, kesinambungan penerapan biopori masih memerlukan dukungan dan pemantauan yang berkelanjutan. Pelatihan lubang resapan biopori terbukti berhasil dalam meningkatkan kesadaran masyarakat mengenai pengelolaan sampah organik yang ramah lingkungan dan berkelanjutan.

title: Penguatan Kapasitas Pengelola Desa Golok sebagai Desa Wisata melalui Literasi Digital dan Partisipasi Warga
abstractText: Desa Mekarmaju di Kabupaten Bandung memiliki potensi wisata berbasis kerajinan pandai besi yang pengembangannya memerlukan pengelolaan informasi digital dan partisipasi masyarakat. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan memperkuat kapasitas pengelola Desa Golok dalam memahami pemanfaatan media digital dan peran masyarakat dalam pengembangan desa wisata. Kegiatan dirancang melalui identifikasi kebutuhan mitra, penyusunan materi pelatihan, perancangan praktik dan pembagian peran, serta pemetaan pemahaman awal peserta. Materi pelatihan mencakup konsep desa wisata, penggunaan Google Maps, media sosial, dan WhatsApp Business, serta peran perajin, warga, dan kelompok sadar wisata (Pokdarwis). Pemahaman awal diukur menggunakan pre-test yang terdiri atas sepuluh soal pilihan ganda. Berdasarkan tabel hasil yang disajikan, seluruh 20 responden menjawab dengan benar setiap butir pertanyaan. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa responden dapat mengenali jawaban yang tepat terhadap konsep-konsep yang diujikan. Namun, hasil pre-test belum dapat menggambarkan keterampilan praktis maupun perubahan pemahaman setelah pelatihan. Evaluasi lanjutan melalui tugas praktik dan pendampingan diperlukan untuk mendukung penerapan media digital serta pembagian peran dalam pengelolaan informasi wisata Desa Golok.

Linear congruence relations for exponents of Borcherds products
abstractText: Abstract For all positive powers of primes $$p\ge 5$$ p ≥ 5 , we prove the existence of infinitely many linear congruences between the exponents of twisted Borcherds products arising from a suitable scalar-valued weight 1/2 weakly holomorphic modular form or a suitable vector-valued harmonic Maaß form. To this end, we work with the logarithmic derivatives of these twisted Borcherds products, and offer various numerical examples of non-trivial linear congruences between them modulo $$p=11$$ p = 11 . In the case of positive powers of primes $$p=2,3$$ p = 2 , 3 , we obtain similar results by multiplying the logarithmic derivative with a Hilbert class polynomial as well as a power of the modular discriminant function. Both results confirm a speculation by Ono.

title: Rethinking Distribution Shifts: Empirical Analysis and Modeling for Tabular Data
abstractText: Different distribution shifts require different interventions, and algorithms must be grounded in the specific shifts they address. However, methodological development for robust algorithms typically relies on structural assumptions that lack empirical validation. Advocating for an empirically grounded data-driven approach to algorithm development, we build an empirical testbed comprising natural shifts across 8 tabular data sets, 172 distribution pairs over 45 methods, and 90,000 method configurations encompassing empirical risk minimization and distributionally robust optimization (DRO) methods. We find that Y|X-shifts are most prevalent in our testbed, in stark contrast to the heavy focus on X (covariate)-shifts in the machine learning literature, and that the performance of robust algorithms is no better than that of vanilla methods. To understand why, we conduct an in-depth empirical analysis of DRO methods and find that underlooked implementation details—such as the choice of underlying model class (e.g., LightGBM) and hyperparameter selection—have a bigger impact on performance than the ambiguity set or its radius. We illustrate via case studies how a data-driven understanding of distribution shifts can provide a new approach to algorithm development. This paper was accepted by Wolfram Wiesemann, data science. title: Climate Risk Disclosure and Risk Sharing in Financial Markets
abstractText: Abstract In this paper, I model how climate risk disclosure impacts climate risk sharing among investors. I show that this disclosure can improve risk sharing by helping investors identify stocks that effectively hedge climate risk, and I analyze the disclosure’s impact on investors’ equilibrium portfolio choices. I then study firms’ voluntary disclosure incentives and analyze when disclosure mandates enhance risk sharing. Finally, I demonstrate that, by facilitating risk sharing, climate risk disclosure reduces the climate risk premium among stocks held by climate-focused investors. Hence, disclosure can lower the valuations of firms with low climate exposures and the overall market. (JEL: D82, D84, G12, G14)

title: FUNDNA software for computing mathematical functions by DNA
abstractText: Introduction Chemical reaction networks (CRNs) are widely used as a design and modeling language for molecular computing and can be compiled into DNA strand-displacement systems. However, designing efficient CRNs for nontrivial mathematical functions remains difficult. Here we present FUNDNA, a software tool that automates the design of CRNs for computing mathematical functions from a high-level user specification. Methods FUNDNA accepts a target single-variable function, computes a Maclaurin-series approximation, rearranges the resulting polynomial using either Horner’s rule or double-NAND expansion, maps the rearranged expression to cascaded molecular AND/NAND units, and outputs the corresponding CRN. The generated CRNs can then be translated to DNA reactions using existing tools. Results We tested the FUNDNA workflow using the 14 function-entry templates available through the software interface and performed DNA-level simulations on four representative eligible examples. The generated rearranged expressions matched their theoretical targets, and the simulated outputs closely tracked the exact function values. Across the reported test cases, the mean square error was below 3.52 × 10 −4 . Discussion FUNDNA provides an accessible workflow for automated design of function-computing CRNs and can help accelerate the development of more complex biomolecular computing circuits.

title: Optimising the early stages of constructed wetland-microbial fuel cell lifecycle: a guide to plant selection, acclimatisation, and start-up
abstractText: ABSTRACT Diagram showing the lifecycle of a constructed wetland–microbial fuel cell (CW-MFC): design, construction, plant adaptation, start-up and operation. Each stage is illustrated with a photograph or drawing beside a central cross-section of a planted cylindrical reactor containing layered gravel and electrodes. Constructed wetland-microbial fuel cells (CW-MFCs) progress through a life cycle from design to operation, during which wastewater is treated and power generated. Research has focussed on the operational phase, overlooking how the earlier phases of plant adaptation and start-up shape performance; the role of plants during these phases remains poorly understood. This study addresses that gap through a step-by-step framework for the initial phases of the CW-MFC life cycle, establishing a baseline that clarifies their function and improves rigour in the field. To the authors' knowledge, it is the first CW-MFC study to combine criterion-based plant selection with a parallel record of biomass development and open-circuit voltage through start-up. Four Australian native species (Phragmites, Juncus, Philydrum and Eleocharis) were selected, adapted, and assessed during start-up. The highest maximum power density was obtained in Juncus cells at 14.4 mW/m2, 4.2 times that of the control (3.45 mW/m2), followed by Phragmites at 12.6 mW/m2. Faster voltage establishment and better performance correlated with biomass growth rather than plant species, highlighting the role of growing plants in enhancing cell voltage and reducing start-up time. The results suggest that voltage output could act as a biosensor for plant biomass growth, although this rests on correlated time trends and requires further testing.

title: An Unfitted Interface Penalty DG-FE Method for Elliptic Interface Problems
abstractText: Abstract. We propose an unfitted interface penalty discontinuous Galerkin–finite element method (UIPDG-FEM) for elliptic interface problems. This hybrid method combines the interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin (IPDG) terms near the interface-enforcing jump conditions via the Nitsche method with standard finite elements away from the interface. The UIPDG-FEM retains the flexibilities of IPDG, particularly simplifying mesh generation around complex interfaces, while avoiding its drawback of an excessive number of global degrees of freedom. We derive optimal convergence rates independent of interface location and establish uniform flux error estimates robust to discontinuous coefficients. To deal with conditioning issues caused by small cut elements, we develop a robust two-dimensional merging algorithm that eliminates such elements entirely, ensuring the condition number of the discretized system remains independent of interface position. A key feature of the algorithm is a novel quantification criterion linking the threshold for small cuts to the product of the maximum interface curvature and the local mesh size. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Reproducibility of computational results. This paper has been awarded the “SIAM Reproducibility Badge: Code and data available” as a recognition that the authors have followed reproducibility principles valued by SISC and the scientific computing community. Code and data that allow readers to reproduce the results in this paper are available at https://github.com/hanjuan339/UIPDG-FEM-for-Elliptic-Interface-Problem.git and in the supplementary materials ( UIPDG-FEM-for-Elliptic-Interface-Problem-main.zip [53KB]). title: Short-term shallow landslide early warning framework integrating radar-based precipitation forecasts and a physically based slope stability model in Taiwan
abstractText: Abstract Taiwan is prone to hillslope disasters in mountain areas because of its special topographical, geological, and hydrological conditions. During typhoons and rainstorms, severe shallow landslides frequently occur. To mitigate the impact of shallow landslides, not only the structural measures are necessary, but also adequate warning systems and contingency measures must be executed. Hence, precise precipitation forecasts and landslide prediction are the most important measures in practice. To account for inherent weather uncertainties precipitation forecasts based on quantitative precipitation forecast model with radar data assimilation method and ensemble mean prediction were adopted in this study instead of using a single model output. The SIMTOP model based on infinite-slope model and TOPMODEL was developed. In considering detail topographic characteristics of the subcatchments, the proposed model can estimate the variation of saturated water level during rainstorms, and then link with the slope instability analysis to clarify whether shallow landslides would occur in the subcatchment. Two area vulnerable to landslide in Taiwan were collected to test the applicability of the model for landslide prediction. Six typhoons events were used to verify the applicability of the proposed model. Four indexes including the probability of detection (POD), false alarm ratio (FAR), threat score (TS), and accuracy (ACC) were adopted to assess the performance of two kinds of very short-term rainfall forecasts with SIMTOP model. The results indicate that quantitative precipitation forecast model with radar data assimilation with SIMTOP model was better than ensemble rainfall forecasts with SIMTOP model. It is promising to apply the proposed model for landslide early warnings to reduce the magnitude of the loss of lives and properties.

title: Fermi-arc-mediated transport in surface Josephson junctions of Weyl semimetals
abstractText: This study presents Fermi-arcs mediated transport in a Weyl semimetal thin slab, interfacing two $s$-wave superconductors. We present detailed study with both time-reversal and inversion symmetry broken Weyl semimetals under grounding, orbital magnetic fields, and Zeeman fields. An orbital magnetic field induces energy level oscillations, while a Zeeman field give rise to the periodic anomalous oscillations in the Josephson current. These anomalous oscillations correlate with the separation of Weyl nodes in momentum space, junction length, and system symmetries. Additionally, we present an explanation by scattering theory modeling the Fermi-arcs as a network model.

Lee-Wave Energy Sinks in Bottom-Intensified Flow
abstractText: Abstract The partition of lee-wave energy sinks in bottom-intensified flows between dissipation and reabsorption is explored over parameter spaces of lee-wave generation frequency, model viscosity, and topographic Froude number. In addition to reabsorption into the sheared mean flow and explicit dissipation by model viscosity, indirect dissipation due to a nonlinear cascade via parametric subharmonic instability (PSI) is identified as a significant but previously overlooked sink that enhances the role of lee waves in dissipating the balanced circulation. This nonlinear energy sink invalidates a previous parameterization for lee-wave reabsorption and dissipation based on wave action conservation. Also, remote dissipation through the generation and radiation of freely propagating internal waves by shear instability near the lee-wave critical layer proves to be negligible. A new parameterization for lee-wave explicit plus indirect dissipation is proposed as a function of lee-wave generation frequency. This parameterization is insensitive to model viscosity and topographic Froude number in the linear and weakly nonlinear generation regimes. For typical broadband, abyssal-hill topographic height spectra at mid- and high latitudes, the net dissipative fraction of the upward lee-wave energy flux from bottom topography is 0.90–0.95, suggesting that reabsorption cannot explain the observed turbulence shortfall in the Southern Ocean.

title: Enhancer-targeted CRISPR-A rescues haploinsufficiency and mutant phenotypes in organoid models of autism
abstractText: Abstract Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a highly heritable condition with diverse clinical presentations. Approximately 15% of the genetic susceptibility of ASD is imparted by de novo haploinsufficient mutations of major effect. We mapped enhancers of two high-confidence autism genes, CHD8 and SCN2A , and used CRISPR-based gene activation targeting enhancers (eCRISPR-A) in human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived excitatory neurons and cerebral forebrain organoids to correct the effects of haploinsufficiency, taking advantage of the presence of a wild-type allele of each gene and endogenous gene regulation. Here we show that eCRISPR-A induced a sustained increase in CHD8 and SCN2A expression specifically in mutant neurons and cortical organoids, with rescue of gene expression levels and mutation-associated phenotypes, including gene expression and physiology. These data support gene activation via targeting enhancers of haploinsufficient genes as a therapeutic intervention in ASD and other neurodevelopmental disorders.

title: Spatial Competition in Fast-Charging Networks
abstractText: Despite the steady growth of fast-charging networks under government subsidies, the impact of spatial and ownership structures of charging points on pricing strategies of charging point operators (CPOs) and consumer welfare is poorly understood. Given EVs’ limited range, the competition in a fast-charging network is inherently regional. It is unclear whether and under what circumstances CPOs’ competition can lead to regional monopoly, which may hinder the transition to electric mobility. In this paper, we develop a novel framework to examine the competitive dynamics in fast-charging networks that serve regional demand, incorporating delay costs arising from congestion and locational attractiveness of charging stations. At the core of our framework is a spatial competition model, which characterizes the strategic interactions between CPOs and consumers. To overcome tractability issues associated with large networks that arise from real-world settings, we propose a computationally efficient method to optimize CPOs’ pricing decisions. We instantiate the framework in Germany’s Deutschlandnetz, whose awarded regional network comprises 900 charging stations. Using demand projections for 2030, we conduct a series of counterfactual simulations. Our analysis generates four sets of findings. First, price exhibits a strong negative correlation with the local competitiveness level (measured by the density of charging stations), but shows no clear dependence on absolute demand levels. Second, CPOs’ profits are shaped by both local competitiveness and absolute demand. Third, a uniform, stringent price cap may create inefficiencies in network utilization and discourage infrastructure investment, particularly in less lucrative regions. Finally, spatial and ownership constraints in tender rules may fail to ensure competitive outcomes in large-scale charging networks, allowing CPOs to strategically select locations that strengthen their market power ex post. Taken together, these findings suggest that policymakers should enable regionally equitable access to fast charging while ensuring efficient network utilization.

title: Influence of aqueous film forming foam containing per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances on the efficiency of activated sludge process and on the composition of the sludge microbiome
abstractText: Abstract The research is part of a project aimed at testing a treatment train to remove per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances commonly known as PFAS, deriving from the foam produced by foam fractionation of aqueous film forming foams (AFFF) contaminated soils. Biological treatment is performed to improve the quality of the resulting foam before destructive treatment. The experimentation was carried out in duplicate in lab-scale bioreactors continuously fed on primary municipal wastewater spiked with increasing doses of AFFF. The results reveal distinct trends: the addition of AFFF did not adversely affect Chemical Oxygen Demand removal, while significantly affecting nitrification efficiency, with inhibition growing with increasing dose. The composition of the microbial community changed with time (especially for Comamonadaceae) and a gradual decline in biodiversity also occurred with time. A decrease in amoA gene bacteria copy numbers and in nitrification efficiency with increasing doses of AFFF were observed.

title: Flat band excitons and quantum metric
abstractText: Abstract We discuss the excitons in flat band systems. Quantum metric plays a central role in determining the properties of single exciton excitations as well as the exciton condensate. While the electrons and holes are supposed to be extremely heavy in flat bands, the excitons (the bound state of an electron-hole pair) could be light and mobile. In particular, we show that the inverse of the effective mass tensor of excitons is proportional to the quantum metric tensor. Meanwhile, the flat band excitons have a finite size, lower bounded by the trace of the quantum metric tensor. Given the properties of single exciton excitation, one can argue for the formation of exciton condensate. Because of the quantum metric, the exciton condensate can support dissipationless counterflow supercurrent, implying the stability of exciton condensate.

title: ENHANCING LEG ENDURANCE USING STRENGTHENING AND AEROBIC EXERCISES
abstractText: The legs, which play a crucial role in balance and coordination, are among the body parts most affected by reduced physical activity, and weak lower-extremity muscles increase the risk of falls and injury. This study determined the effectiveness of strengthening and aerobic exercises in enhancing the leg endurance of first-year college students. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design was employed with eighty-four (84) students, aged 18 to 20, from a state university campus in Bukidnon, Philippines, who were divided into two groups of 42. Group A performed strengthening exercises (wall squats, leg extensions, and lunges), while Group B performed aerobic exercises (jogging, jumping rope, and jumping jacks) twice a week for six weeks. Leg endurance was measured with the wall squat test before and after the interventions, and the data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and paired and independent samples t-tests at the 0.01 level of significance. Results showed that the leg endurance of both groups improved significantly from pretest to posttest (strengthening group: t = 7.53, p < .01; aerobic group: t = 5.63, p < .01). The increment of the aerobic exercise group (M = 103.12) was significantly higher than that of the strengthening exercise group (M = 51.83), t = −2.62, p = .010. The study concludes that both strengthening and aerobic exercises are effective interventions for enhancing leg endurance and may be integrated into Physical Education classes. This research adds to the limited literature on improving leg endurance through strengthening and aerobic training in the Philippines.

title: Anti-lipase induced anti-obesity effect of ethanol extract of Syzygium cumini and Dioscoria bulbifera plants in rat model: An integration between pharmacological and computational approaches
abstractText: Objective While the anti-obesity potential of Syzygium cumini has been previously reported, the pancreatic lipase-inhibitory mechanism of S. cumini and Dioscorea bulbifera has not been explored. This study provides the first integrated pharmacological-computational investigation of the anti-obesity potential of ethanol extracts from S. cumini seeds and D. bulbifera roots in a high-fat diet (HFD)-induced rat model. Methods Ethanolic extracts of S. cumini seeds and D. bulbifera roots were prepared, filtered, and dried using a rotary evaporator. In vitro antioxidant activity was assessed via total phenolic content (TPC) and DPPH free radical scavenging (IC 50 values). Anti-lipase activity was evaluated against porcine pancreatic lipase (PPL) and compared to Orlistat. In vivo effects were tested in HFD-induced white albino Wistar rats (8−9 weeks old, (110 ± 8) g) at 500 mg/kg body weight for 12 weeks, monitoring body weight and lipid parameters (triglycerides [TG], cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein [HDL], and low-density lipoprotein [LDL]) versus Orlistat (10 mg/kg). Lipase inhibitory mechanisms were explored via in silico molecular docking. Results TPC was (103.79 ± 3.45) mg GAE/g for S. cumini and (69.31 ± 2.99) mg GAE/g for D. bulbifera extracts. DPPH IC 50 values were (93.03 ± 6.23) μg/mL ( S. cumini ), (177.13 ± 7.52) μg/mL ( D. bulbifera ), and (10.84 ± 0.92) μg/mL (butylated hydroxytoluene, BHT, used as the reference antioxidant). Both extracts significantly ( P < 0.05) reduced body weight in HFD rats compared to Orlistat. At 1.0 mg/mL, S. cumini and D. bulbifera extracts inhibited 60.84% and 54.59% PPL activity, respectively, versus 95.71% for Orlistat (0.1 mg/mL), concentrations that were not equivalent, reflecting the substantially higher potency of purified Orlistat relative to the crude plant extracts. Both extracts and Orlistat significantly ( P < 0.05) lowered elevated TG, LDL, and cholesterol. Molecular Docking showed Quercetin and Isoquercetin binding to rat lipase at the Orlistat binding site with high affinity. Conclusion Ethanol extracts of S. cumini seeds and D. bulbifera roots reduced body weight and improved lipid profiles in HFD rats; in vitro anti-lipase inhibition and in silico docking suggest pancreatic lipase inhibition as one plausible contributing mechanism.

title: Soil storage and growth media shape culture-based recovery of pyrophilous bacteria and fungi from burned soils
abstractText: Increasingly frequent and severe fires worldwide underscore the need to understand how pyrophilous microbes survive, thrive, and drive post-fire ecosystem regeneration. However, characterizing their traits through omics and phenotypic assays is limited by the lack of cultured isolates. Here, we collected burned soils after a severe California shrubland wildfire and used a culturomics approach to test how culture media type and soil storage method affected the abundance and diversity of pyrophilous bacteria and fungi. Using fresh soils, we compared three media types: rich media (Lysogeny Broth [LB] for bacteria; Malt Yeast Agar [MYA] for fungi), oligotrophic Reasoner’s 2A (R2A), and a newly developed pyrogenic organic matter (PyOM) media. We also evaluated four soil storage methods using rich media: air-drying, refrigeration at 4°C, and freezing at –80°C with or without glycerol. R2A recovered the greatest richness of bacterial and fungal genera, although PyOM medium isolated several taxa not recovered on other media. For bacteria, freezing soils at –80°C without glycerol preserved the greatest genus richness, whereas freezing with glycerol preserved the greatest species richness. For fungi, freezing at –80°C without glycerol preserved the most species while maintaining genus richness comparable to fresh and refrigerated soils. These findings guided the development of a culture collection of more than 500 pyrophilous bacterial and fungal isolates. Lessons learned from media type and soil storage can also be applied to the cultivation of environmental soil microbes from many habitat types and improve culture collections of fastidious microbes.

title: Sleep promotes sublexical learning and clears out by-products of word recognition
abstractText: Most models of spoken word recognition include both lexical and sublexical representations. When speech input is consistent with a given lexical or sublexical representation, that representation’s activation increases, with recognition dependent on reaching some absolute or relative activation level. After a representation has been activated during perception, it remains sensitive to similar subsequent input for some period of time. In the current study we report four experiments that investigate the time course of this increased sensitivity, with sleep as a potential moderating factor. The experiments show that the sensitivity of sublexical representations remains elevated for at least 15-20 minutes, but less than 12 hours, if the listener is awake during this time; if instead sleep follows the activation of sublexical representations, the increase in sensitivity continues for at least 12 hours. Elevated sensitivity of sublexical representations facilitates processing of other pseudowords that contain these sounds. In contrast, active lexical representations impair processing of pseudowords that only differ by one segment. Such impairment is observed after delays of 12 hours without sleep, but not if the 12 hours includes sleep; sleep appears to clear out already-established representations. Our findings demonstrate that sublexical and lexical representations, once engaged during speech perception, become more sensitive to subsequent similar input, with the durability of the sensitivity differing as a function of lexical status and wake/sleep after the initial perceptual exposure.

title: Top pruning and phosphorus fertilization improve female cone yield potential and modify nitrogen and phosphorus allocation in grafted Pinus massoniana clones
abstractText: Abstract Top pruning is an effective way to produce "orchard-style" forest seed orchards, and phosphorus (P) fertilization can improve the reproductive ability of Masson pine (Pinus massoniana) to some extent. However, it is necessary to determine the absorption and distribution of carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) nutrients by applying phosphorus fertilizer under top pruning. Two clones, high-yielding (209) and low-yielding (225), were tested in a pot experiment with 15N markers during early floral primordium. Calcium magnesium phosphate fertilizer was applied at doses of 0 g/plant (P0), 200 g/plant (P2), and 400 g/plant (P4) to the test plots without top pruning (N-TP) and with top pruning (TP). Overall, top pruning promoted female cone formation in high-yielding P. massoniana clones and significantly affected the downward movement of the fruiting layer, the density of female cones in the lower branches increased by 25.45%~64.97% after top pruning. However, their impact on the formation of female cones in low-yield clones was limited. Top pruning altered the variation of C:N, N:P ratios by increasing C, N and P contents of lower branches. Compared with no top pruning, the C:N ratios of lower branches of 209 and 225 clones increased by 5.79%~27.38% and 2.57%~13.60% after top pruning, respectively. At flowering period, the distribution ratios of N and P in high-yielding female cones increased by 175.0% and 46.3% after top pruning, respectively, indicating that top pruning promoted the absorption of N and P content to female cones. The interaction effect between top pruning and P fertilizer had a significant impact on female cone density, The application of P fertilizer can improve the N harvesting ability of P. massoniana under top-pruning measures, especially by increasing the C:N ratio in the second layer of coniferous branches in the lower part of the tree and promoting the distribution of N to female flower heads, which is beneficial for improving seed yield. On the whole, top pruning causes changes in the spatial structure of trees, affecting the redistribution of nutrients and promoting the distribution of N and P to female cones; The application of phosphorus fertilizer not only regulates the carbon to nitrogen ratio of needles, but also improves the N and P nutrient absorption capacity of P. massoniana under the combination of top pruning measures, which helps to distribute nutrients to organs related to the formation of female cones. The study confirmed that top pruning and phosphorus fertilization increased the probability of high yield and altered the nutrient distribution characteristics in P. massoniana.

title: Recreational Runners' Sense of Smell and Taste After a Race: On the Acute Impact of Endurance Running on Chemosensory Perception
abstractText: ABSTRACT Several studies suggest that endurance exercise can directly enhance chemosensory functions. There already is empirical evidence indicating that frequent physical exercise may enhance (or maintain) taste and smell function. The central aim of the current study was to further examine the acute effects of endurance running on taste and smell recognition in a sample of recreational runners. A total of 61 recreational runners were recruited via convenience sampling. Taste and smell recognition was tested once directly after a run (either 10 km or 21 km) and once at rest. Further, on both occasions, all participants rated sweet taste intensity and salty taste intensity as well as their liking for both sweet and salty taste. After running, sweet taste recognition was poorer than at rest. Relative to sweet taste, salty taste intensity was significantly increased after running. Smell identification did not differ between rest and after the run.

title: Enumeration of all superconducting circuits up to 5 nodes
abstractText: Nonlinear superconducting circuits can be used as amplifiers, transducers, and qubits. Only a handful have been analyzed or built, so useful configurations likely remain undiscovered. In this paper, we enumerate all unique nonlinear superconducting circuits, up to five nodes in size, built of capacitors, inductors, and Josephson junctions. We catalog the resulting design space by sorting circuits into "Hamiltonian classes" using a set of reference coordinates. Finally, we search for novel superconducting qubits by explicitly considering all three-node circuits, showing how the results of our enumeration can be used as a starting point for circuit design tasks.

title: The Data-Driven Censored Newsvendor Problem
abstractText: We study a censored variant of the data-driven newsvendor problem, where the decision maker must select an ordering quantity that minimizes expected overage and underage costs based only on offline censored sales data rather than historical demand realizations. Our goal is to understand how the degree of historical demand censoring affects the performance of any learning algorithm for this problem. To isolate this impact, we adopt a distributionally robust optimization framework, evaluating policies according to their worst-case regret over an ambiguity set of distributions. This set is defined by the largest historical order quantity (the observable boundary of the data set), and contains all distributions matching the true demand distribution up to this boundary while allowing them to be arbitrary afterward. We demonstrate a spectrum of achievability under demand censoring by deriving a natural necessary and sufficient condition under which vanishing regret is an achievable goal. In regimes in which it is not, we exactly characterize the information loss due to censoring: an insurmountable lower bound on the performance of any policy, even when the decision maker has access to infinitely many demand samples. We then leverage these sharp characterizations to propose a natural robust algorithm that adapts to the historical level of demand censoring. We derive finite-sample guarantees for this algorithm across all possible censoring regimes and show its near-optimality with matching lower bounds (up to polylogarithmic factors). We moreover demonstrate its robust performance via extensive numerical experiments on both synthetic and real-world data sets. This paper was accepted by Wolfram Wiesemann, data science. title: Gfa2bin enables graph-based GWAS by converting genome graphs to pan-genomic genotypes
abstractText: Variation graphs offer superior representation of genomic diversity compared to traditional linear reference genomes, capturing complex features, especially structural variants, that are otherwise inaccessible to analysis. Given the known role of structural variants in functional allelic variation, it seems self-evident that exploiting variation graphs for genome-wide association studies (GWAS) should enable more comprehensive knowledge of associations between genetic variants and phenotypic traits. We present a tool, gfa2bin, that offers multiple methods to (i) use variation graphs for genotyping, and (ii) convert the genotypes into well-established data formats for use in GWAS. In a case study where we apply gfa2bin to Arabidopsis thaliana, we demonstrate with 1,695 traits that variation graphs can detect genotype-phenotype associations not found with linear reference genomes. Our approach complements SNP-based methods; not only does graph-based GWAS produce additional associations, but associations also found with SNPs have on average higher significance in graph-based GWAS. gfa2bin is implemented in Rust, and commented source code is available under an MIT license at https://github.com/MoinSebi/gfa2bin. Examples of how to run gfa2bin are provided in the documentation. We provide several Python scripts and a Snakemake pipeline for easy use of the tool with larger data sets. The packing tool (https://github.com/MoinSebi/packing) is recommended for reduced storage and preprocessing (normalization) of sequence-to-graph alignments.

title: An Onsager-type theorem for general 2D active scalar equations
Predominance of viral core functions over auxiliary metabolism among carbohydrate-active enzymes annotated in the global soil virosphere
abstractText: Soil viruses are increasingly recognized as components of microbial communities with the potential to alter ecosystem functioning, yet the frequency and functional distribution of virus-encoded metabolic genes in soils remain poorly understood. Here, the Global Soil Virus Atlas gene catalog, comprising 1,432,147 viral genes from 1,223 samples across 12 ecosystem types, was searched against KEGG, Pfam, and CAZy for functions related to carbon cycling, nitrogen cycling, and antimicrobial resistance. Annotations associated with host entry or cell-wall lysis were separated from putative auxiliary metabolic functions. Of 5,020 initial gene-level functional annotations across the three categories, 3,322 (66.2%) were classified as peptidoglycanases. Their exclusion left 1,698 genes (0.14% of the gene catalog restricted to contigs ≥10 kb), and carbon-cycling functions represented 96.7% of the enzyme-resolved annotations. Chitinase-associated genes formed the largest carbon category, but 78.0% belonged to GH19, a family containing both chitinases and phage endolysins. Among GH19 genes on contigs encoding detectable holins or spanins, 84.2% occurred within three genes of these lysis components, a distribution comparable to that of canonical phage lysozymes. Across six matched metagenomic studies, estimated viral contributions to the targeted functions ranged from 0.00% to 8.45% (mean: 2.27%). Two of the three estimates exceeding 2% were GH19-associated chitinase estimates from rhizosphere soils and were therefore treated as upper estimates. Thus, the putative soil viral metabolic inventory was sparse and concentrated in carbon-degradation functions, whereas much of the initial carbohydrate-active enzyme signal reflected core viral lysis functions rather than auxiliary metabolism. IMPORTANCE: Soil microorganisms drive decomposition and nutrient cycling, and the viruses that infect them may alter these processes by carrying genes that affect host metabolism. However, genes annotated as carbohydrate-degradation enzymes may instead help viruses enter cells or break host cell walls when new virus particles are released. In a worldwide catalog of soil viruses, approximately two-thirds of the initial functional assignments represented these infection or release activities. After their removal, putative viral auxiliary metabolic genes were uncommon and concentrated mainly in carbon degradation. Genes potentially involved in chitin degradation were most frequent, but many occurred near viral genes used to break host cells; their estimated contribution should therefore be viewed as an upper limit. Distinguishing core viral functions from host metabolic modification is essential to avoid overestimating viral contributions to soil processes and to identify the strongest candidates for experimental testing.

title: Contextualizing biological heterogeneity in brain structural normativity assessments across the aging continuum with the nearest neighbor normativity framework
abstractText: Abstract Background: Despite established consensus about the individuality of brain physiology and structural changes, current neuroimaging biomarker paradigms heavily rely on population averages. Here, we define normativity not as a single reference point but as a landscape of permissible configurations arising from diverse physiological manifestations. Methods: We introduce the Nearest Neighbor Normativity (N 3 ) framework, designed to parse the natural heterogeneity in brain structural measurements into a diversity-aware biomarker of brain structural decline. Through repeated comparisons within different demographic subgroups, N 3 contextualizes an individual’s measurements from several viewpoints along the aging continuum. Relying on local density estimation, it accommodates multiple, shared normative configurations within and across age groups. We use T1-weighted MRI data from 29,883 individuals for training and 7,013 individuals for validation, and benchmark our framework against Brain Age models and Normative Modeling. We evaluate each biomarker’s ability to detect neurodegenerative diseases, using them as representative models of atypical brain structural decline. Results: In group-level analyses, the N 3 biomarker shows the largest effect sizes in the detection of Mild Cognitive Impairment, Alzheimer’s Disease, and Frontotemporal Dementia. Similarly, the N 3 biomarker achieves the highest predictive performance in the classification of neurodegenerative diseases on a single subject level. Notably, the N 3 estimates remain stable across age and robust to compositional changes in the reference sample. Finally, correlation analyses indicate that it captures distinct and complementary aspects of brain structural variation compared to existing approaches. Conclusions: Our findings underscore that rethinking normativity assessments to explicitly accommodate natural inter-individual variability can advance our collective efforts toward truly personalized patient care.

title: Epithelium stratifies via nucleation and growth induced by foam-geometric instability
abstractText: Abstract Epithelial stratification, the transition from a monolayer to a multilayer structure, occurs across a wide range of phenomena. Recent studies have identified several cell behaviors as triggers, including junctional tension, cell density and geometry, and topological defects. However, how these factors drive stratification throughout the entire epithelium remains poorly understood. Here, we show that epithelial stratification proceeds through a nucleation-and-growth mechanism. Combining cell culture with three-dimensional vertex modeling, we demonstrate that multilayer origins emerge in a dispersed manner and expand across the epithelium through disordered intermediate states. This transition is induced by a mechanical instability inherent in the foam-like geometry of the epithelium. Moreover, the nucleation-growth concept applies to embryonic skin development and intestinal cancer transformation. These findings conceptualize epithelial stratification as a form of structural transition governed by foam mechanics, offering a physical perspective on various epithelial developments.

title: Optimizing Feature Selection in Causal Inference: A Three-Stage Computational Framework for Unbiased Estimation
abstractText: Feature selection is an important but challenging task in causal inference for obtaining unbiased estimates of causal quantities. Properly selected features in causal inference not only significantly reduce the time for matching algorithms but, more importantly, reduce the bias and variance when estimating causal quantities. When feature selection techniques are applied in causal inference, the crucial criterion is to select variables that, when used for matching, can achieve an unbiased and robust estimation of causal quantities. Recent research suggests that balancing only on treatment-associated variables introduces bias while balancing on spurious variables increases variance. To address this issue, we propose an enhanced three-stage framework that demonstrates significant improvements in selecting the desired subset of variables compared to the state-of-the-art feature selection framework for causal inference, resulting in lower bias and variance in estimating causal quantities. We evaluated our proposed framework using state-of-the-art synthetic datasets across various settings and observed superior performance with reasonable computational cost, demonstrating scalability for large-scale datasets. Finally, to demonstrate the applicability of our proposed methodology using large-scale real-world data, we evaluated our framework on several real-world public datasets.

title: Impact of HIV infection, immune status, and integrase inhibitor-based antiretroviral therapy on the gut microbiota in men who have sex with men with and without HIV
abstractText: ABSTRACT Background HIV infection and antiretroviral therapy (ART) influence gut microbiota, affecting inflammation, immune function, and systemic health. However, isolating the effects of integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI)-based ART on gut microbiota is complicated by confounding factors, including HIV status, immunosuppression, and sexual behavior. Methods This study examined three cohorts of men who have sex with men (MSM): 1) HIV-negative individuals using post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) (n=22), 2) PWH with <350 CD4 cells/μL before and after ART (n=21 and n=13, respectively), 3) PWH on long-term INSTI-based ART with >500 CD4 cells/μL (n=17). Fecal microbiota was analyzed through 16S rRNA sequencing, with functional profiling using PICRUSt2. To compare differences in bacterial abundance and functions, we used ANCOM-BC2. Results PWH showed significantly lower alpha diversity than HIV-negative participants, especially those with marked immunosuppression. Short-term ART in PEP users showed no significant impact microbiota, while beta diversity clustered by HIV status rather than ART exposure. Pro-inflammatory taxa, such as Prevotellaceae, were enriched in PWH, reflecting interactions between HIV and MSM status. Functional profiling indicated elevated genes linked to antibiotic resistance, metabolism, and stress in PWH. While INSTI-based ART caused minor functional changes, it increased beneficial genera like Barnesiella . Conclusions While HIV significantly disrupts gut microbiota, INSTI-based ART preserves microbial diversity and community structure. Complementary microbiota-targeted interventions could enhance health outcomes for PWH.
