title: Perinatal maternal and child growth mediate the association between maternal education and children’s overweight/obesity in Europe: the Feel4Diabetes-study
abstractText: Abstract Background/Objectives: Early-life factors and maternal education interact with childhood overweight/obesity through pathways that remain unclear. Our aim was to investigate the predominant perinatal correlates of childhood overweight/obesity and their mediating effects on the association between maternal education and children's overweight/obesity. Subjects/Methods: In this cross-sectional study the total sample included 12211 children (4–12 years-old) from low socioeconomic status (SES) regions in six European countries, with 2663 having complete data for analysis. Interventions/methods: All measurements were carried out during August-September 2016. Children’s anthropometrics were measured and parents self-reported all other data (perinatal/ sociodemographic) via questionnaires. All variables were adjusted for maternal education, sex and age (p<0.05). Results: Maternal overweight (OR 1.54 (95% CI 1.19–1.99)), obesity (OR 2.51 (95% CI 1.57–4.00)), pre-pregnancy diabetes (OR 4.92 (95% CI 1.31–18.38)), smoking during pregnancy (OR 1.59 (95% CI 1.20–2.10)) and excessive gestational weight gain (OR 2.00 (95% CI 2.59–2.53)) were associated with childhood overweight/obesity. Children born small-for-gestational-age (OR 0.57 (95% CI 0.36–0.89)) had lower odds, whereas those born long-for-gestational-age (OR 1.49 (95% CI 1.15–1.92)) had higher odds of childhood overweight/obesity. Rapid weight gain during the first 6 months was positively associated (OR 1.30 (95% CI 1.04–1.63)) with overweight/obesity in children. Maternal pre-pregnancy weight status, rapid weight gain in the first 6 months and gestational weight gain mediated by 16.6%, 8.4%, and 7.8%, respectively, the maternal education-child obesity link. Conclusion: Perinatal factors play a crucial role in the onset of childhood obesity, and evidence suggests their association with maternal education. Families with lower education should be targeted, aiming to raise awareness of health issues related to maternal/children’s healthy lifestyle and improve nutrition knowledge, aiming to ensure healthy maternal weight prior to and during pregnancy and normal infant growth.

title: G-quadruplex profiling using single-cell CUT&Tag offers insight into the epigenetic landscape of the developing mouse brain
abstractText: Abstract Background G-quadruplexes (G4s) are non-canonical DNA structures that have gained increasing attention for their potential roles in gene regulation and role in neurodegenerative diseases and cancer. Despite their biological significance, G4 structures have not been studied systematically across tissues and cell types. Results In this study, we employ G4 single-cell CUT&Tag (G4 scCUT&Tag) to characterize G4 landscapes in postnatal mouse brain cells, leveraging single-cell analytical approaches commonly used in scRNA-Seq and scATAC-Seq datasets. Using conventional single-cell omics workflows to process and explore our data, we distinguish distinct cell lineages based on G4 heterogeneity and establish that a subset of lineage-specific genes show unique promoter G4s. Multi-omics integration with scRNA-Seq gene expression profiles, using both a covariance-based technique (canonical correlation analysis) and a transfer learning-based approach, enables more accurate cell-type annotation. These integrations not only reveal correlations between G4 signal and gene expression, but demonstrate that G4 scCUT&Tag enables detailed examination of G4 heterogeneity in complex tissues and supports integrative analysis of G4 profiles with other omics layers, offering new insights into the epigenomic landscapes of the developing brain. Conclusions Our findings establish G4 scCUT&Tag as a framework for investigating the cellular heterogeneity of G4 landscapes in complex tissues and provide a basis for exploring their relationships with gene regulation and other layers of chromatin organization.

title: Laser-guided ion dynamics in a dual-mode memristor for bioinspired neuronal and synaptic integration
abstractText: Abstract Neuromorphic computing aims to replicate the parallel, adaptive nature of biological intelligence in electronic systems. Despite considerable advances in memristor technology, material-encoded neurosynaptic bifunctionality has not been demonstrated. We introduce a laser-guided dual-mode memristor that integrates both volatility for neuronal spiking and nonvolatility for synaptic plasticity within a single-phase material. By precisely modulating silver ion dynamics through XeCl excimer laser irradiation, we achieve local and dynamic control of the dual-mode memristive behavior without requiring a heterogeneous device array or stacking. The neurosynaptic tunability with optimal computational efficiency demonstrates reconfigurable reservoir computing and a positive feedback loop for adaptive learning.

title: The Digital Journey of Health Insurance Marketing: Narrative Ads and Product Page Design
abstractText: Selling health insurance through digital advertising is fundamentally different from selling most consumer products online: health insurance protects against abstract future risks, and regulatory constraints prohibit transactions from closing on third-party platforms, forcing consumers to transition from the ad platform to the insurer’s own product page. We examine how aligning narrative ad content with product page design sustains persuasion across this mandatory handoff. In a randomized field experiment with a leading Chinese insurer on Douyin, we study 335 ads that generated nearly 17 million impressions and 777,412 click-throughs. Users who clicked were randomly routed to either a fact-based product page or one incorporating a customer experience exemplar. Purchase conversion rises most when narrative ads are paired with the exemplar page, increasing from 1.51% to 2.05%, implying roughly 8,400 additional policies per month at campaign scale. Neither element is effective in isolation. A causal mediation analysis confirms that sustained engagement on the product page accounts for more than 80% of the total effect. To address algorithm-driven selection in ad delivery and self-selection into clicking, we employ a sequential endogeneity correction strategy and confirm robustness with causal forests. Aligning ad design with product page design significantly improves conversion in regulated digital markets. History: Catherine Tucker served as the senior editor. Funding: X. title: Pre-clinical medical students’ perception of surgical professions and balance with personal life – a single-centre exploratory analysis
abstractText: Abstract Background Surgical professions deal with serious challenges to inspire students to pursue a surgical career and counteract demographic change. Students’ interest in sub-specialization is influenced by socio-economic factors including work-life balance, flexible working hours and appreciation. However, robust data about the current perception of surgical professions in the early stage of medical education is lacking so far. Methods We performed a voluntary online survey among students who participated in an elective neurosurgical course during their preclinical stage of medical studies. The investigator-developed survey addressed perception of unspecified surgical professions, including personal requirements, profession impact on health and lifestyle and the topic of gender disparities and family planning and was conducted before the students entered their elective course. We also assessed viewpoints on support programs facilitating compatibility of surgical training and family life. Results A total of 109 students participated in the voluntary survey (66.1% female, 33.0% male, 0.9% not specified). Overall, 56.0% of respondents reported prior experience with surgical professions and 33.9% planned to pursue a surgical career. Most respondents (68.8%) rated surgical professions as more physically demanding than other specialties, and about half (49.5%) considered them more harmful to physicians’ health. In contrast, only 26.6% rated the mental burden as higher in surgical than in other specialties. In the exploratory gender comparison, female participants more often agreed that male residents have better career chances in surgery, whereas male participants more often responded neutrally to this statement. Overall, 89.0% of participants expressed interest in unspecified support programs to improve the compatibility of professional and personal life, and 65.1% would be willing to accept a one-year extension of their surgical residency. Conclusions In summary, pre-clinical medical students of a preselected cohort tend to rate surgical disciplines as demanding, competitive and difficult to balance with private life. Most participants expressed interest in support programs for combining surgical training and family life which needs further evaluation in future studies.

title: Polymer dynamics reveal stage-wise unfolding and homologous pairing of chromosomes in fission yeast
abstractText: During meiosis, the exchange of genetic material ("recombination") is essential to bring about genetic variation in offspring. To carry out the recombination, homologous pairs of DNA have to come into proximity and align, which is inherently a polymer dynamics problem. In fission yeast, this is accomplished by the extensive nuclear oscillation that applies a pulling force on the chromosome polymers. In this work, we investigate the competition between the pulling force that tries to facilitate the alignment and the intra-chromatin interactions that assist the chromatin folding. The crucial role played by the intra-chromatin interaction for a range of pulling forces and loci locations is highlighted here. Upon comparing our results with the experimental findings, we not only reaffirm the enhancement of contact probability with loci-dependent pulling but also get a meaningful interpretation of the chromosome unfolding and pairing at different stages of movement.

title: The zoo of the gene networks capable of pattern formation by extracellular signaling
abstractText: A fundamental question of developmental biology is pattern formation, or how cells with specific gene expression end up in specific locations in the body to form tissues, organs, and, overall functional anatomy. Pattern formation involves communication through extracellular signals and complex intracellular gene networks integrating these signals to determine cell responses (e.g. further signaling, cell division, cell differentiation, etc.). In this article, we address two questions: (1) Are there any logical or mathematical principles determining which gene network topologies can lead to pattern formation by cell signaling over space in multicellular systems? (2) Can gene network topologies be classified into a small number of classes that entail similar dynamics and pattern transformation capacities? We combine logical arguments and mathematical proofs to show that, despite the large amount of formally possible gene network topologies, all gene network topologies capable of pattern formation fall into only three fundamental classes and their combinations. Additionally, we show that gene networks within each class share the same logic on how they lead to pattern formation, and hence, lead to similar patterns. We characterize the main features of each class. This zoo includes the complete gene networks that, to the best of our knowledge, have been experimentally reported to lead to pattern formation as well as other gene networks that have not yet been found experimentally.

title: Development and characterization of a larp7 knockout zebrafish model for alazami syndrome
abstractText: Alazami syndrome (AS) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by severe growth restriction, significantly impaired intellectual development, microcephaly, and distinctive facial features, caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in the LARP7 gene. However, the phenotype remains poorly defined due to the limited number of reported cases and the impact of its defects on human health is not yet fully understood. We reported a case with AS, reviewed all previously reported 48 AS patients, and generated a zebrafish knockout of the l arp7 gene. This patient was compound heterozygous for two pathological variants. Among these AS patients, the main clinical manifestations included intellectual disability (56/56), motor developmental delay (55/55), facial dysmorphism (50/50), short stature (50/54), low weight (36/45), and microcephaly (28/46). More than half also exhibited fetal growth retardation and behavioral abnormalities. These affected individuals all had bi-allelic pathogenic, loss-of-function variants in LARP7 . The larp7 -/- zebrafish showed reduced body length, smaller eye intervals at 3, 4 and 5 days post-fertilization and decreased distance and average velocity. Larval locomotion tests indicated impaired activity and response to stimuli, while open field tests revealed elevated anxiety levels. Transcriptome analysis identified increased aberrant splicing events in larp7 -/- zebrafish, linked to AS patient phenotypes. AS is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder with severe growth restriction and microcephaly. This study establishes and validates the larp7 -/- zebrafish as an animal model to study AS in vivo, offering a valuable tool for further elucidation of larp7 precise mechanism in the development of this disease and the identification of potential therapeutic targets.

title: Stochastic Programming for Dynamic Temperature Control of Refrigerated Road Transport
abstractText: Temperature control in refrigerated delivery vehicles is critical for preserving product quality, yet existing approaches neglect critical operational uncertainties, such as stochastic door-opening durations and heterogeneous initial product temperatures. We propose a framework to optimize cooling policies for refrigerated trucks on fixed routes by explicitly modeling these uncertainties while capturing all relevant thermodynamic interactions in the trailer. To this end, we integrate high-fidelity thermodynamic modeling with a multistage stochastic programming formulation and solve the resulting problem using stochastic dual dynamic programming. In cooperation with industry partners and based on real-world data, we set up computational experiments that demonstrate that our stochastic policy consistently outperforms the best deterministic benchmark by 35% on average as well as a rolling two-stage approach while being computationally tractable. In a separate analysis, we show that by fixing the duration of temperature violations, our policy operates with up to 40% less fuel than deterministic policies. Our results demonstrate that pallet-level thermal status information is the single most crucial piece of information in the problem and that it can be used to significantly reduce temperature violations. Knowledge of the timing and length of customer stops is the second-most important factor, and together with detailed modeling of thermodynamic interactions, it can be used to further significantly reduce violations. Our analysis of the optimal stochastic cooling policy reveals that preemptive cooling before a stop is the key element of an optimal policy. These findings highlight the value of sophisticated control strategies in maintaining the quality of perishable products while reducing the carbon footprint of the industry and improving operational efficiency. title: Arousal state fluctuations destabilize speech intelligibility in older adults
abstractText: Understanding speech in noisy, multi-talker environments is fundamental for social communication but becomes increasingly challenging as we age. Age-related hearing loss reduces audibility and degrades speech encoding, yet these deficits do not fully explain the momentary lapses in speech understanding that frustrate real-time communication. Here, we tested whether brain state fluctuations immediately before speech onset predict forthcoming speech recognition errors in older listeners. We measured the accuracy, speed, and consistency of speech recognition in 183 adults aged 18-76 years (103 female) using a brief, trial-based multi-talker listening task while tracking pupil dynamics before and during speech presentation. Prestimulus pupil-linked arousal predicted trial-level speech recognition in older, but not younger, adults, independent of hearing status, cognitive load, and task accuracy. In adults over 50 years of age, lower and higher extremes of prestimulus pupil size were associated with less accurate and slower responses, producing a striking inverted-U relationship between prestimulus arousal and forthcoming behavioral performance. Older adults exhibited lower extremes of pupil-linked arousal that were specifically associated with greater self-reported difficulty listening in everyday life. By contrast, stimulus-evoked pupil dilation during speech encoding, a measure of listening effort, did not predict trial-level performance at any age. These findings identify prestimulus pupil-linked arousal as a hidden marker of forthcoming lapses in speech intelligibility in older adults. When considered alongside conventional measures of peripheral hearing status in mixed-effects regression models, these measures provide a more complete accounting of biological changes underlying speech intelligibility deficits that frustrate social communication in older adults . Significance statement As we age, following a conversation in crowded environments becomes more difficult and frustrating, even when hearing tests appear normal. This study shows that fluctuations in arousal level (measured through prestimulus pupil size) are tightly linked to fluctuations in the speed and accuracy of speech processing in adults over 50 years of age. Changes in arousal state regulation uniquely accounted for the moment-to-moment variations in speech intelligibility and were more closely associated with self-reported listening challenges than other conventional measures. These findings highlight the contribution of brain-wide arousal systems to real-world listening challenges and identify a straightforward measure that could be used to more comprehensively assess and potentially improve speech understanding in social settings.

title: Outlier-Robust Multi-Group Gaussian Mixture Modeling with Flexible Group Reassignment
abstractText: Do expert-defined or diagnostically-labeled data groups align with clusters inferred through statistical modeling? If not, where do discrepancies between predefined labels and model-based groupings occur and why? In this work, we introduce the multi-group Gaussian mixture model (MG-GMM), the first model developed to investigate these questions. It incorporates prior group information while allowing flexibility to reassign observations to alternative groups based on data-driven evidence. We achieve this by modeling the observations of each group as arising not from a single distribution, but from a Gaussian mixture comprising all group-specific distributions. Moreover, our model offers robustness against cellwise outliers that may obscure or distort the underlying group structure. We propose a novel penalized likelihood approach, called cellMG-GMM, to jointly estimate mixture probabilities, location and scale parameters of the MG-GMM, and detect outliers through a penalty term on the number of flagged cellwise outliers in the objective function. We show that our estimator has good breakdown properties in presence of cellwise outliers. We develop a computationally-efficient EM-based algorithm for cellMG-GMM, and demonstrate its strong performance in identifying and diagnosing observations at the intersection of multiple groups through simulations and diverse applications in medicine and oenology.

title: Fresh tephra deposits from the Tajogaite Volcano boost thermophile proliferation and soil organic matter recovery
abstractText: Tephra fallout deposition during volcanic eruptions overlays existing soils, profoundly altering their physical, chemical, and biological properties. This study investigates the impact of the newly deposited tephra blanket from the 2021 Tajogaite eruption (La Palma Island) on the molecular composition of soil organic matter and microbial diversity across different soil horizons. To our knowledge, this is the first study combining molecular pyrolysis, stable isotope analysis, and microbial sequencing to characterize the early biogeochemical transformation of soils affected by the Tajogaite eruption. A combination of 16S rRNA gene sequencing, pyrolysis-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (Py-GC/MS), and elemental and isotope ratio mass spectrometry (EA/IRMS) was employed. Our results reveal marked differences in organic matter composition and microbial community structure across the tephra-covered soil profile, with patterns consistent with ongoing microbial transformation of organic carbon and nitrogen compounds. The soil horizon directly beneath the tephra layer (horizon O) displayed a higher abundance of labile organic compounds and a reduced presence of recalcitrant compounds compared to the deeper horizons (A and Bw). This pattern is strongly associated with the predominance of thermophilic bacteria, which contribute actively to the breakdown of complex organic materials such as lignin and hydrocarbons, and drive key biogeochemical processes including nitrogen and carbon cycling. The continuous geothermal influence of nearby fumaroles further supports the persistence and ecological success of thermophilic communities in these volcanic soils. These findings underscore the critical role of volcanic activity not only in reshaping soil structure but also in enhancing soil fertility and resilience through microbial-mediated processes. Understanding these dynamics is essential for soil management and ecosystem recovery strategies in volcanic regions, providing new insights into the long-term effects of tephra deposition on soil health and the carbon cycle.

title: Epigenetic alterations in the placenta associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy
abstractText: Abstract Histone modifications play a key role in chromatin organization and transcriptional regulatory potential. Previously, reduced levels of trimethylated histone H3K4me3 and acetylated H3K9ac were observed in placentas from women with preeclampsia. Building on these findings, this study investigated whether SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy or at delivery is associated with changes in placental histone modifications. Immunohistochemical staining, exploratory western blot analysis, and qualitative immunofluorescence were performed on placental sections from 60 patients stratified into four groups: women with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection at delivery, women with prior infection during gestation, vaccinated controls, and unvaccinated controls. H3K4me3 levels in the syncytiotrophoblast were significantly reduced in both SARS-CoV-2-exposed groups compared to unvaccinated controls, with the most pronounced reduction observed in women with prior infection during gestation. H3K9ac levels did not differ significantly between groups in any compartment after correction for multiple comparisons. No significant associations were found between SCT H3K4me3 levels and maternal age, gestational age, or birthweight, and a sensitivity analysis excluding cases with additional placental pathologies confirmed the robustness of the findings. As no gene expression profiling was performed, functional or transcriptional consequences of the observed H3K4me3 changes cannot be inferred. These descriptive findings warrant further investigation integrating epigenetic and transcriptomic approaches to clarify their functional relevance for placental biology and pregnancy outcomes.

title: Noncanonical enhancers control gene expression and cell fate in human pluripotent stem cells
abstractText: Enhancers are key gene regulatory elements that ensure the precise spatiotemporal execution of developmental gene expression programs. However, recent findings indicate that current approaches to identify enhancers may not capture the full repertoire of active enhancers in mammalian genomes. Here, we combine massively parallel enhancer assays with chromatin structure and transcriptome profiling to functionally annotate enhancers genome-wide in human induced pluripotent stem cells. We find that a substantial fraction (∼40%) of accessible chromatin regions with enhancer function lack key features associated with active enhancers, including the active enhancer mark histone H3 lysine-27 acetylation and enhancer-associated RNAs. Perturbation of this class of noncanonical enhancers by CRISPR-mediated epigenome editing or deletion results in decreased levels of target gene expression and, in one instance, loss of pluripotent stem cell characteristics. Collectively, our data demonstrate enhancer activity for a class of gene regulatory elements that had, until now, only been associated with a neutral or inactive status, challenging current models of enhancer function.

title: Seeing the forest through the traits: a four-dimensional framework for modeling and measuring latent user traits
Configuring strategic action: a comparative study of top management teams and the microfoundations of strategy
abstractText: Purpose This study examines how and why practitioners, practices and praxis (3Ps) become configured differently across contrasting organizational contexts. Through a comparative study of a university hospital and a private hospital, it investigates how organizational and institutional conditions shape practitioner agency, the function of formal and informal practices, the direction of strategic activity and the meanings attached to strategy work in reliability-seeking organizations. Design/methodology/approach We employ a qualitative comparative case-study design, drawing on 57 semi-structured interviews, archival documents and observational data from a state-affiliated university hospital and a privately owned hospital group located in Antalya, Türkiye. Data were analyzed through an abductive process combining inductive within-case thematic analysis with theoretically informed cross-case comparison. Findings Similar committees, reports, informal interactions and analytical tools produced distinct configurations of strategic action because authority, evaluative criteria, temporal pressures and knowledge were organized differently. In the university hospital, layered authority, professional legitimacy and long-tenured knowledge carriers combined custodial agency with institutional sensemaking; operational issues therefore moved upward for formal authorization, producing upward legitimization. In the private hospital, competitive pressure, market-facing knowledge, founder-centered selection authority and performance- and risk-based evaluation combined entrepreneurial agency with emergent sensemaking; strategic initiatives circulated laterally across functional boundaries before centralized approval and operationalization, producing lateral initiation. Research limitations/implications The two-case design supports analytical rather than statistical generalization. The identified configurations and underlying mechanisms provide a theoretically specified basis for comparison across other reliability-sensitive and institutionally contrasting settings. Practical implications Managers should design strategic processes that enable permeability between formal and informal arenas, recognize multiple forms of practitioner agency and treat strategy implementation as an ongoing sensemaking process rather than a linear execution phase. Originality/value This study makes three theoretical contributions. First, it theorizes the Strategy-as-Practice 3Ps as contextually patterned configurations. Second, it identifies upward legitimization and lateral initiation as distinct mechanisms connecting formal and informal strategy work. Third, it explains how decision authority, evaluative criteria, temporal pressures and knowledge distribution generate different combinations of practitioner agency, practice functions and sensemaking.

title: The operational 3DEnVar data assimilation scheme for the Météo-France convective scale model AROME-France
abstractText: Since October 2024 the Météo-France operational convective scale model AROME-France has been using a 3DEnVar data assimilation (DA) scheme in order to improve the performance of severe weather prediction. This paper describes the configuration and evaluation of this 3DEnVar scheme. It summarizes the work carried out to configure this scheme in an operational context, with the inherent constraints of numerical robustness, compatible execution times, and of course correct performance of the forecasts produced. The adjustment of horizontal and vertical localization, inflation, hybridization, and the use of Incremental Analysis Updates (IAU) are studied in sensitivity experiments, and the impact on the spin-up is investigated. A configuration and its variation with IAU are thus defined and evaluated using different scores over a long period and on different severe meteorological situations (winter storms, fog, and High Precipitating Events): they largely outperform the operational 3D-Var. The version with IAU was implemented in the new operational version of the AROME-France assimilation system.

title: Expression and activity of prolactin receptor isoforms in non-malignant and malignant lung cells
abstractText: Abstract Background In the last years, it has been noticed the participation of prolactin in different malignancies such as breast and prostate cancer. Recently, prolactin (PRL) was proposed as a biomarker for lung cancer but its molecular mechanisms remain to be explored in this tissue. The aim of this work was to assess prolactin receptor (PRLR) isoforms expression in lung cell lines and its effects in cell viability, proliferation and pathways activation in normal and lung cancer cell lines. Methods and Results PRLR was assessed by WB and immunofluorescence, cell proliferation was performed using MTT assay and STAT5 activation was assessed using WB to detect p-STAT5 and immunofluorescence to explore p-STAT5 nuclear translocation. We found differential expression of PRLR isoforms which were localized differentially in cellular compartments in lung cancer cell lines A549 and SK-LU-1 and in the normal lung cell line BEAS-2B. We did not observe significant differences in cell viability after PRL administration at low doses, however, an augmented viability was found at high doses of PRL treatment. Importantly, at low doses of PRL, we observed an increase in p-STAT5 and its translocation to the nucleus. Conclusions The overall results suggest that PRL may play a differential role in lung cancer cells via STAT5 activation by using different PRLR isoforms. However, further studies are needed to stablish its role in lung carcinogenesis.

title: DNA uptake and twitching motility are controlled by small RNA Arp through repression of pilin translation in Acinetobacter baumannii
abstractText: Acinetobacter baumannii is a major opportunistic pathogen capable of natural transformation. This process is driven by type IV pili (T4P) facilitating horizontal gene transfer and accelerating the spread of antimicrobial resistance. While the transcriptional regulation of T4P is increasingly understood, post-transcriptional mechanisms controlling pilus assembly remain unexplored. Here, we identify and mechanistically characterise a small RNA, Arp ( Acinetobacter repressor of pilin), as a post-transcriptional repressor of T4P-mediated functions in A. baumannii . Previous proximity RNA-RNA ligation experiments using High throughput Global sRNA target Identification by Ligation and Sequencing (Hi-GRIL-seq), indicated interactions between Arp and the 5′ end of the pilA mRNA, encoding the major pilin subunit PilA. Here, in-line probing and translational reporter assays revealed that Arp represses pilA translation in A. baumannii by sequestering the Shine-Dalgarno sequence and the first seven codons of the pilA mRNA. Accordingly, deletion of arp increases DNA uptake and twitching motility, while overexpression of Arp depletes pilA mRNA from A. baumannii cells significantly impairing DNA uptake and twitching motility—two hallmark T4P-dependent phenotypes. Together, our study identifies a native A. baumannii sRNA that modulates natural competence by targeting pilin synthesis, revealing a new regulatory layer that could be exploited to disrupt horizontal gene transfer in multidrug-resistant strains.

title: Novel insights into the specialized metabolism of the extremophile black yeast Hortaea werneckii and its modulation, unlocking its potential for compound discovery
abstractText: Hortaea werneckii is a halotolerant yeast, found in various habitats and which specialized metabolism remains largely unexplored. Moreover, its chemical response to high salinities has not been thoroughly investigated. To address this gap, a large-scale metabolomic study based on HPLC-HRMS/MS was conducted on 64 strains, collected from different habitats worldwide, and cultivated both on saline and non-saline media. The culture media salinity significantly modulated the strains metabolomes, suggesting the yeast exhibits a specific chemical response to high salt concentrations, potentially linked to halotolerance mechanisms. Additionally, the metabolomes were influenced by the ecological origin of the strains, with opportunistic pathogenic isolates producing distinct metabolites. Molecular networking revealed that H. werneckii synthesizes various chemical classes, including potential cytotoxic compounds, making this yeast a potentially interesting source of bioactive compounds. Hortein was detected as dominant and ubiquitous, emerging as a potential chemical marker for the species. This study highlights several compounds of interest, related to the chemical ecology and pathogenicity of H. werneckii . As most of them remain unidentified, future research should prioritize their isolation and identification, to improve our understanding of this extremophile organism and harness its potential in natural product discovery.

title: Entangled stoichiometric objectives shape microbial catabolism
abstractText: The understanding of fundamental relationships between energetic and biosynthetic parameters of catabolism and anabolism is a central challenge in microbiology. The large diversity of microbial metabolisms can be compared on the basis of our current definitions of catabolism and anabolism. Catabolism has two functions: synthesising charged energy carriers and carbon precursors. Energy carriers, however, are also involved in precursor synthesis, complicating the analysis. We introduce an unbiased method to quantify stoichiometric relationships between catabolism and anabolism in genome-scale metabolic models. We compare catabolic strategies across diverse (heterotrophic) microbial species and growth conditions, focusing on states of maximal biomass yield per unit of energy source. Catabolic networks turn out to vary greatly, due to variation in the energy and carbon source for growth and the requirement to make suitable precursors for anabolism. We find that the ATP requirement for 1 gram biomass ranges between 72.8 and 148.0 mmol, precursor sets range between 4 and 14 in size, and acetyl-CoA is the only universal precursor across species. An important varying factor is the amount of ATP that is produced or consumed during precursor synthesis. This causes the remaining ATP demand, which is produced in catabolism, to vary. We conclude that the diversity of heterotrophic catabolism results from entanglement between charging of energy carriers and precursor synthesis. The state of maximal energetic efficiency is reached by maximizing the yield of charged energy carriers during precursor synthesis and simultaneously minimizing the demand for charged energy carriers in the conversion of precursors into macromolecules. Our formal analysis of catabolic diversity using a rigorous definition of catabolism’s two functions shows that microbial metabolism cannot be simplified in this manner; it rather shows that these two functions are intertwined due to the precise biochemistry.

title: Mobile phone use while driving and associated factors: an observational study in Córdoba, Argentina
abstractText: OBJECTIVE: Mobile phone use while driving (MPWD) is a growing road safety concern. This observational study explores handheld MPWD and associated factors in the city of Córdoba, Argentina. METHODS: gun radar), and handheld mobile phone use. Factors associated with handheld mobile phone use (yes/not) were analyzed using a multiple logistic regression model. RESULTS: The observed percentage of mobile phone use was 4.6%. The logistic regression results indicate higher usage among young adult drivers (18-24 years), delivery motorcycle riders, and those driving light and heavy cargo vehicles. Additionally, mobile phone use was more prevalent on weekdays and during afternoon hours, compared to the morning. Greater use was also noted on major urban roads rather than local streets, and during periods of lower traffic count. On average, drivers using mobile phones traveled at lower speeds. CONCLUSIONS: MPWD was linked to human, environmental, and situational factors. Drivers seem to regulate when and where they use their phones and exhibit risk-compensatory behaviors, such as reducing speed. Young drivers and those who drive for work should be priority targets for prevention campaigns.

title: Industrialization, class conflict, and the closing window of democratic opportunity
abstractText: Abstract This paper addresses two long-standing questions in the political economy of development: how the timing of industrialization affects the transition to democracy and how different social classes shape that transition. We develop a sequential game among landed elites, industrialists, and workers embedded in a growth model with endogenous industrialization. The model identifies a window of democratic opportunity during which the industrial class prefers democracy to industrial autocracy. Whether democracy occurs depends on two dimensions of workers’ de facto political power: their power against the landed class determines when industrialization occurs and when landed rule ends; their power against the industrial class determines when the democratic window closes. Later industrialization therefore makes democratization less likely but not impossible. A calibration to Great Britain and numerical exercises for early and late industrializers show that the revolt threat required to sustain democracy rises as industrialization is delayed. Faster technological growth advances political transitions but does not, by itself, determine whether democracy or industrial autocracy follows landed rule.

title: A qualitative assessment of perceived resilience in agricultural marketing cooperatives
abstractText: Agricultural marketing cooperatives are vital to agricultural systems, yet their resilience remains understudied. This research applies and extends the resilience assessment framework for farm systems to these cooperatives, examining robustness, adaptability, transformability, and anticipation. Using a qualitative approach, we conducted in-depth interviews with 18 German cooperative decision-makers from December 2023 to February 2024 to examine their perceptions of resilience. Our study employs thematic analysis and deductive category formation to investigate the framework's applicability, gain insights into perceived resilience capacities and strategies, and examine how cooperative values are perceived to foster resilience through the resilience capacities. Results show the adapted framework effectively captures unique cooperative aspects from the perspective of interviewees. Respondents generally describe their organizations as robust and diversified, and as maintaining resilience through adaptability in business fields and functions. While overall resilience is perceived as high, individual capacities vary, with robustness rated highest and anticipatory capacity lowest. Cooperative values are viewed by respondents as contributing to resilience, especially during crises, but are also described as facing challenges. This study provides one of the first systematic qualitative analyses of perceived resilience in agricultural marketing cooperatives and contributes to understanding factors that may support stability and sustainability in food systems.

title: Assessing Early-Stage Net CO 2 Fluxes From Soils and Maize Plants During a Short-Term Enhanced Weathering Mesocosm Trial
abstractText: It is becoming increasingly accepted that annual gigatonne-scale carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) removal, in conjunction with rapid decarbonization, is necessary to meet international climate goals and limit global warming below 2 °C. This will require the development and rapid scaling of new forms of carbon management. When developing new carbon dioxide removal (CDR) techniques, complete accounting of how the process affects greenhouse gas fluxes is essential. Enhanced weathering (EW), the spreading of weatherable, cation-rich crushed rocks to soils, has the potential to sequester significant amounts of CO 2 while improving soil health. Yet, the effect that increases in soil pH from EW has on soil organic carbon (SOC) decomposition remains debated. A potential concern is that increasing soil pH can lead to enhanced SOC remineralization, although more data is needed. Additionally, many studies do not measure CO 2 fluxes continuously, capture net top-of-column CO 2 fluxes, or monitor established key levers on CO 2 emission from soils. To add to this debate, we present soil carbon pool data from a ~3 month time series encompassing sequential net CO 2 flux experiments from an EW greenhouse study in large mesocosms. We focused on mildly acidic soils where, on short time scales, cations from weathering quantitively moved into the exchangeable fraction. Therefore, gas flux changes in this system should be largely linked to changes in organic carbon (SOC stores and plant processes). We find no significant correlation between CO 2 fluxes and soil pH and no significant correlation between CO 2 fluxes and rock application. Although this does not rule out a link between soil pH and SOC remineralization rates, the effect is small relative to other factors, like temperature and soil moisture. Although minor increases in total inorganic carbon were observed in basalt-amended soils, these increases did not support a direct link between soil pH and increased CO 2 emissions.

title: Approximating Transition Dynamics with Discrete Choice
Nitrogen and Phosphorus Losses in a Rural Watershed Under no Tillage System in Southern Brazil
abstractText: ABSTRACT Intensive production is sought by farmers but may compromise sustainability depending on management. No‐Tillage System (NTS) is a conservation system and paradigm in Brazilian grain production; however, the quality of its adoption is questioned as water erosion regained importance and remains underestimated. This study quantified nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) concentrations and losses and evaluated the seasonal contribution of soluble and particulate fractions to nutrient export in a rural watershed under long‐term NTS without terraces in southern Brazil. A 118.8‐ha watershed comprising 13 agricultural fields was monitored from December 2022 to November 2023. Streamflow was continuously monitored at the watershed outlet, while daily streamwater samples were collected and analyzed for total, soluble, and particulate N and P. Nitrate (N‐NO 3 − ) and ammonium (N‐NH 4 + ) concentrations remained below the Brazilian critical environmental limit (CEL), whereas TP frequently exceeded the 0.10 mg L −1 threshold. Particulate N (PN) accounted for 70.20% of total N (TN) export, while particulate P (PP) accounted for 97.65% of total P (TP) export, demonstrating the predominance of particulate pathways. Nutrient losses increased markedly during intense precipitation and high streamflow, particularly in October and November. Annual losses reached 30.80 kg N ha −1 and 4.91 kg P ha −1 , corresponding to monetary losses of US$ 22.58 ha −1 and US$ 4.85 ha −1 , respectively. Overall, long‐term NTS alone was insufficient to prevent substantial nutrient losses under high‐flow conditions, particularly in particulate form. Integrating NTS with mechanical runoff control practices and effective soil cover is therefore essential to improve soil and water conservation in agricultural watersheds.

title: Inferring the history of gene copy number evolution
abstractText: Gene duplication plays a crucial role in the adaptive evolution and diversification of organisms by creating extra copies of genes that can evolve new functions while preserving the original. Duplicated genes can become fixed in populations or appear as copy number variants. However, inferring and dating these duplication events from present-day data is challenging, as gene copy count distributions could result from either a few ancient duplication events or many recent ones. Sequence based phylogenetic reconstruction, an often seen practice, does not include the history of individuals and hence may result in inconsistencies and subsequent misinterpretations. Here, we introduce a novel model for inferring gene copy number evolution, which describes gene duplication and their evolution over time through a random walk on a coalescent duplication network. This approach is solely based on copy number counts and hence independent of the inconsistencies of sequence based inferences. Backward in time we implement structured coalescent simulations, where we re-interprete 'structure' as 'genealogical distance' based on copy number counts. We apply this model to the NB-ARC domain counts of NLR genes in A. thaliana to infer the number and times of duplication events that have led to the present day copy number distribution.

title: Spatial modelling of available aluminum in glacial till: informing a boreal forest soil carbon predictor
abstractText: Boreal forest soils store 30 % of global forest soil carbon, making them a crucial component of the carbon cycle. However, climate change at high latitudes is increasing temperatures and producing unpredictable precipitation patterns. Soil organic carbon (SOC) formation and stabilization is tied to precipitation patterns, thus climate change will inevitably influence the stability and longevity of boreal forest SOC. The current size and distribution of this reservoir is poorly understood, creating uncertainty under current and future climate scenarios. Previous research demonstrates mineral soil properties may be used to model boreal forest SOC accurately. The surface slope, depth of carbon enriched horizon, and climate characteristics are important parameters for modelling SOC and can generally be obtained or estimated via remote sensing. However, information about the availability of reactive aluminum – non-crystalline forms capable of interacting with organic matter to form stable carbon rich organometal complexes in mineral soils – is not widely available but is controlled by the weatherable aluminum in soil parent material. To bridge this gap, the Newfoundland and Labrador till geochemistry dataset was used here to map and model weatherable aluminum availability in glacial till across the island of Newfoundland as a function of geology and climate. The Random Forest Algorithm was employed to develop two models: one relying solely on the strength of geological and climatic variables, and the other drawing additionally on the spatial context of sample points. The first model performed well ( R 2 =0.60), however, adding a spatial component increased the performance of the second model ( R 2 =0.71). Bedrock type and proximity of the samples to certain units were indicated to be the strongest controls on aluminum availability, while environmental factors were less influential. Additionally, model uncertainty was calibrated empirically and mapped spatially, providing reliable and actionable information about the confidence of predictions over the study area. This project demonstrates the value of predictive geospatial modelling for till geochemistry mapping and delivers key aluminum availability predictions useful for future efforts in deriving SOC reservoir estimates across Newfoundland.

title: Tackling Estimation Risk in Kelly Investing Using Options
abstractText: The Kelly criterion provides a general framework for optimizing the growth rate of an investment portfolio over time by maximizing the expected logarithmic utility of wealth. However, the optimality condition of the Kelly criterion is highly sensitive to accurate estimates of the probabilities and investment payoffs. Estimation risk can lead to greatly suboptimal portfolios. In a binomial model, we show that the introduction of a European option generates a family of alternative replications of the same log-optimal terminal payoff. Under the misspecification of the payoff, these replications respond differently to model error, allowing combinations of option-based strategies that improve realized long-run growth relative to the standard Kelly strategy.

title: Five elements of psychological support in disaster recovery during the COVID-19 pandemic in Victoria, Australia between 2020 and 2022
abstractText: The COVID-19 pandemic and associated public health interventions had profound effects on mental health worldwide. Pandemic preparedness must incorporate strategies to support mental health and psychological recovery, which should be underpinned by the five essential elements of disaster recovery – safety, calm, efficacy, connectedness, and hope. Residents of Victoria, Australia, experienced stringent non-pharmaceutical public health interventions to mitigate the spread of COVID-19 and associated health and health system impacts. Data from seven cross-sectional surveys of adults (the CARE Study) between April 2020 and April 2022 was used to explore how anxiety, depression, and the five elements presented in Victorians over time. Multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) was utilised to understand the essential elements most closely related to mental health. Symptoms of depression and anxiety fluctuated over the pandemic, peaking in September 2021, when Victoria was midway through an 82-day long lockdown. This coincided with lowest observed levels of efficacy, hope, and connectedness. Anxiety symptoms were lowest in May 2020, when participants’ efficacy, hope and connectedness were highest. MCA results suggest that a stronger sense of efficacy, hope and connectedness was associated with lower anxiety and depression. Conversely, high levels of anxiety and depression were associated with lower efficacy, less hope, and feeling disconnected. These results highlight efficacy, connectedness and hope as key targets for mental health interventions in outbreak scenarios. Further work is required to understand the nuances of resilience and psychological response in the context of a pandemic, to facilitate rapid identification of at-risk groups and tailor effective, targeted interventions.

title: A concurrent working memory task disrupts motor performance but preserves adaptation during dexterous object manipulation
abstractText: Abstract Dexterous everyday actions such as grasping and lifting objects rely on precise sensorimotor control and are often performed under concurrent cognitive demands. This study examined how cognitive load induced through a verbal working memory task affects sensorimotor integration in anticipatory adaptation during object manipulation. Participants adapted to an asymmetrical mass distribution by generating compensatory moments at object lift onset, with the aim of minimising object roll. Sensorimotor adaptation performance and grip force modulation were assessed under both single-task (motor only) and dual-task (motor plus working memory) conditions. Results showed that cognitive load led to longer reaction times and increased grip forces, indicating cognitive-motor interference consistent with previous literature. Crucially, however, the trajectory of the adaptation to the novel object dynamics remained robust even under high cognitive load. This resilience suggests that the core processes of error-driven, trial-by-trial motor adaptation which hinge on salient, task-relevant visual and haptic feedback, are relatively immune to the disruptive effects of concurrent working memory demands.

title: Development and internal validation of the RLF score for predicting pentafecta achievement after robot-assisted partial nephrectomy
abstractText: Precise prediction of perioperative outcomes for robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN), a cornerstone treatment for localized renal cell carcinoma (RCC), requires optimization. While the R.E.N.A.L. nephrometry score quantifies tumor anatomy and the Mayo Adhesive Probability (MAP) score assesses perinephric adhesion risk, their predictive efficacy remains debated. This study aimed to develop and validate a novel predictive model to guide RAPN clinical decision-making. A retrospective analysis was conducted on 704 patients undergoing primary RAPN for unilateral tumors at Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital between 2018 and 2023. Preoperative computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) images were evaluated in consensus by three physicians (two urologists and one radiologist), blinded to clinical outcomes, to obtain R.E.N.A.L. (Radius, Exophytic/endophytic, Nearness to collecting system, Location relative to polar lines) and MAP (Fat Thickness, Fat Stranding) parameters. The primary endpoint was Pentafecta achievement, defined as Trifecta (negative surgical margin, absence of Clavien-Dindo ≥ grade III complications, ≤ 30% decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR)) plus intraoperative estimated blood loss (EBL) ≤ 50 mL and operative time (OT) ≤ 150 min. Multivariate regression identified independent predictors used to construct the RLF scoring system. Model performance was validated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Pentafecta was achieved in 258 of 704 patients (36.6%). Multivariate linear regression identified R (β = 23.95, P < 0.001), L (β = 9.63, P < 0.001), and FS (β = 9.57, P < 0.001) as core predictors of OT. R (β = 49.79, P < 0.001) and FS (β = 13.64, P < 0.001) were independent predictors of EBL. Multivariate logistic regression confirmed R (odds ratio (OR) = 1.60, P = 0.011), L (OR = 1.48, P = 0.014), and FS (OR = 1.35, P < 0.001) as independent predictors of Trifecta failure. Furthermore, R (OR = 2.99, P < 0.001), L (OR = 2.06, P < 0.001), and FS (OR = 1.88, P < 0.001) were identified as independent predictors of Pentafecta non-achievement. The RLF score, integrating R, L, and FS, demonstrated significantly superior predictive efficacy for Pentafecta (AUC = 0.78, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.75–0.81 ) compared to the R.E.N.A.L. score (AUC = 0.71, 95% CI: 0.67–0.75 ) and MAP score (AUC = 0.70, 95% CI: 0.66–0.74 ). At the optimal cutoff value of 0.587, sensitivity was 0.69, specificity was 0.75, and the negative predictive value (NPV) was 0.81. Calibration curves and the Hosmer-Lemeshow test ( P = 0.760) indicated good model fit. The RLF score, the first simplified model integrating R (tumor diameter), L (polar location), and FS (fat stranding) from R.E.N.A.L. and MAP scores, effectively stratifies perioperative risk for RAPN. A predicted probability above the cutoff identifies high-risk patients with 81% certainty, supporting intensified preoperative preparation, whereas patients below the cutoff show markedly better perioperative outcomes, providing an evidence-based framework for personalized surgical management. The model’s reliance on fundamental anatomical parameters suggests potential for broader applicability.

title: Supporting Community Health Workers During Extreme Heat: CFIR–ERIC Guided Scoping Review of Implementation Strategies
abstractText: Abstract Background Community health workers (CHWs) are essential to healthcare delivery in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) yet face increasing threats from extreme heat events (EHEs) due to climate change. Occupational health policies for CHWs remain fragmented globally, with CHWs receiving less attention than workers in other industries despite their critical frontline role. This scoping review aimed to identify barriers and facilitators affecting CHWs during EHEs and determine implementation strategies to support heat safety. Methods We conducted a scoping review by performing a systematic search across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and grey literature published between 2000 and 2024, yielding 1,386 records. After screening, 20 studies met the inclusion criteria. Data synthesis applied the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to categorize barriers and facilitators, while the CFIR-ERIC matching tool mapped these to implementation strategies from the Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change (ERIC) taxonomy. Results CHWs in LMICs are central to climate-health responses, and also uniquely vulnerable to heat exposure. Widespread barriers to safe and effective service delivery during EHEs include physical challenges (such as dehydration, heat stress, and exhaustion), psychological stress linked to community expectations, inadequate infrastructure (notably poor cooling and inconsistent utilities), chronic underfunding restricting salaries and supplies, insufficient climate-health training, limited policymaker awareness of heat-health issues, and poor community health-seeking behaviors. Key facilitators that support CHWs include their strong community commitment and trust, deep contextual knowledge, disaster preparedness capabilities, and growing grassroots engagement in heat resilience efforts. However, CHWs remain frequently excluded from intervention design and strategic decision-making. The review identified 43 ERIC implementation strategies tailored to address the unique challenges and opportunities for supporting CHWs during EHEs. Of these, 65% served dual functions: mitigating barriers and reinforcing facilitators. Top-priority cross-cutting strategies included resource-sharing agreements, continuous training, promoting system adaptability, offering clinical supervision, creating educational materials, and coalition-building among stakeholders. Conclusions Many implementation strategies exist to both facilitate CHWs’ responding during EHEs and to protect them during those events. However, success depends on contextual adaptation, with interventions addressing local heat-health risks and socio-political contexts. These findings underline the need to take action to support CHWs during EHEs.

title: Smart strategy for built environment optimization: In-situ test and orthogonal experiment in traditional ethnic dwellings
abstractText: Maintaining indoor thermal comfort usually increases energy consumption from HVAC systems, making the development of passive retrofit strategies important. This study focuses on traditional dwellings in the cold high-altitude region of northwestern Sichuan, China, aiming to balance thermal performance improvement with the preservation of their architectural and cultural value. Field measurements, simulation modeling, standardized scoring, orthogonal experimental design, and simulation validation were integrated to evaluate passive retrofit strategies. The orthogonal experiment reduced the full-factorial design space from 8,748 possible combinations to 81 representative cases. The optimal strategy was identified as building form A, orientation S360, SEPS wall insulation, window construction 5, and WWR i. This strategy increased the proportion of thermally comfortable hours from 7.8 % in the baseline case to 24.0 %, corresponding to an increase of 16.2 percentage points. The study demonstrates that indoor thermal comfort in traditional dwellings in cold high-altitude regions can be substantially improved while preserving architectural appearance and cultural value. The findings provide a transferable methodological reference for traditional dwellings facing the dual challenge of heritage conservation and thermal performance improvement.

title: Impact of long-term home and community use of a lower limb sensory neuroprosthesis
abstractText: Abstract Background Individuals with lower limb loss experience sensorimotor deficits that often lead to adoption of compensatory gait strategies, which increase their risk of developing secondary comorbidities, reduce balance confidence, and negatively impact functional abilities. Despite advancements in prosthetic technology, current devices lack direct sensory feedback that replicates the somatosensation once provided by the missing foot. This study examines how long-term home and community use of a sensory neuroprosthesis (SNP) designed to provide real-time plantar sensory feedback through implanted nerve cuff technology affects functional performance, balance confidence, and quality of life. Methods A 68-year-old individual with unilateral transtibial limb loss utilized the system in home and community environments for 9.5-months to perform normal daily activities, while returning to the laboratory periodically to complete various functional and qualitative assessments. Outcomes included Timed Up and Go ground reaction force metrics and completion and stance times, Functional Gait Assessment scores, stair negotiation strategy and error frequency, self-reported stumbles and falls, usage diaries, and semi-structured interviews. Results Prosthetic limb propulsive impulse increased significantly, with higher values observed during the Active SNP phase compared to the Pre-Active and Post-Active phases when plantar sensory feedback was not provided at home. Prosthetic-to-intact limb propulsion symmetry improved from 43​78% during the Pre-Active phase to 89–95% during the Active phase, before declining to 65–72% during the Post-Active phase. TUG completion and stance times varied across assessments but showed limited and inconsistent differences between active and inactive SNP conditions. FGA scores remained high throughout the trial, with highest scores achieved at Pre-Active 1 and Active 1 when the SNP was active. During 4-inch stair negotiation with obstructed visual feedback, the participant showed changes in lead foot preference during ascent, decreased compensatory use of heel probing during descent, and exhibited a reduction in error frequency after the initial Pre-Active assessment. Self-reported stumble frequency declined from 7 stumbles/week at the end of the Pre-Active phase to 2 stumbles/week by the conclusion of the Active phase. The SNP was used 135 of the 214 days of the Active phase, corresponding to a 63.1% usage rate. The semi-structured interviews revealed that plantar sensations at lower perceived intensities were more comfortable and functionally useful, and that prolonged home SNP use enabled confident perception of prosthetic foot-ground contact without the need to employ previously utilized compensatory strategies of increased socket loading to infer foot placement. Conclusions These findings offer compelling evidence that home use of the SNP may reduce reliance on compensatory gait mechanics, potentially lower fall risk, and improve user confidence in diverse and uncontrolled real-world environments. title: Unravelling groundwater's role in soil-plant-atmosphere continuum: integrated ecohydrological modelling approach using STEMMUS-SCOPE and MODFLOW 6
abstractText: Soil-plant-atmosphere continuum (SPAC) models are commonly used to investigate various components' role(s) in ecosystem functioning. Yet, in most SPAC models, groundwater is ignored or at best represented in an over-simplified manner, leading to misunderstanding of its critical role in simulating soil-vegetation dynamics. This study investigates groundwater's role in SPAC processes, in particular, the impacts of groundwater component (mass and energy) on: (1) regulating the soil profile, in terms of moisture and temperature; (2) the dynamics of the unsaturated/saturated zones and their further impact on water fluxes; and (3) the carbon fluxes and vegetation physiological processes (i.e. root water uptake and photosynthesis reflected by fluorescence). To address this, an integrated ecohydrological modelling (IEM) framework is developed by coupling the STEMMUS-SCOPE SPAC model with the MODFLOW 6 integrated hydrological model. The standalone STEMMUS-SCOPE (ST-SC) and the coupled STEMMUS-SCOPE-MODFLOW 6 (ST-SC-MF6) models were applied over an 8-year period (1 April 2016–31 March 2024) to three sites in the Netherlands (Loobos, Cabauw and Veenkampen). Various essential variables, including soil moisture ( θ ), soil temperature ( T s ), groundwater level (GWL), groundwater temperature (GT), evapotranspiration (ET), gross primary productivity (GPP), net ecosystem exchange (NEE), and sun-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF) were simulated and then compared to corresponding in-situ observations. Performance of both ST-SC and ST-SC-MF6 was evaluated using the Kling–Gupta efficiency (KGE) and the root mean square error (RMSE) metrics. Results indicated that the groundwater contribution is spatially and temporally variable. The ST-SC-MF6 model showed better agreement with observations than the ST-SC, improving the KGE values for: (a) θ (+0.29), T s (+0.19), and ET (+0.35) at Loobos, (b) θ (+0.30), T s (+0.14), NEE (+0.18), and SIF (+0.15) at Cabauw, and (c) θ (+0.21) and ET (+0.15) at Veenkampen. Notably, benefits of ST-SC-MF6 simulation were particularly prominent during both wet and dry periods, i.e. improving the representation of: (a) the θ dynamics during wet conditions, when hydraulic connectivity between the phreatic surface and the unsaturated zone is strong; (b) the root water uptake and carbon assimilation during dry periods, when shallow groundwater mitigated vegetative water stress; and (c) the T s dynamics during both wet and dry periods, influenced by both GT and GWL, and further propagated to other T s -dependent processes/variables such as canopy temperature. Overall, the proposed ST-SC-MF6 IEM helped to: (1) incorporate groundwater as a key component of the water, energy and carbon cycles; and (2) define the important role groundwater dynamics plays in the SPAC for deepening the understanding of ecosystem functioning.

title: Sea fennel (Crithmum maritimum L.) powder as a complete substitute for added sodium chloride in harissa, a UNESCO-listed heritage condiment: sodium reduction, consumer acceptability, and sensory trade-offs
abstractText: Abstract Harissa, the Tunisian red-pepper paste inscribed on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, is traditionally seasoned and preserved with added salt, and condiments of this kind contribute substantially to dietary sodium in North Africa. This study asked whether the added salt can be removed in its entirety and replaced with dried, powdered aerial parts of the Mediterranean halophyte sea fennel. Four pastes were prepared in triplicate, retorted in glass jars, and compared: an unsalted control, a conventionally salted control, and two formulations in which no salt was added and sea fennel powder was incorporated at two and at three grams per hundred grams. Physicochemical composition, surface colour, pigment and radical-scavenging measurements, microbial counts, accelerated thermal stability, real-time ambient storage, macronutrient composition, and sensory properties were determined, and sodium was estimated by mass balance rather than from chloride titration. Chloride and estimated sodium fell substantially, which supports a reduced-sodium but not a low-sodium claim. The enriched pastes were darker and redder, stayed within their usual acidity range, and were ranked above the salted control by a blind consumer panel, at the cost of lower perceived saltiness and higher bitterness. The product remains a low-acid canned food whose safety rests on the scheduled thermal process.

title: Do More Visitors Mean More Crime? Analyzing the Impact of Visitor Patterns on Crime Rates in Urban Areas Using Mobile Device Foot Traffic Data
abstractText: Abstract This spatial inquiry addresses a key question in routine activity theory: does an influx of visitors into a neighborhood increase crime opportunities by increasing the number of motivated offenders and suitable targets, or does it enhance guardianship capacity? The study explores these dynamics across different crime types: aggravated assault, robbery, and motor vehicle theft using more accurate cell phone mobility data to estimate work-hour and after work hour visitors in Arlington, TX. Results from spatially lagged negative binomial regression models reveal that higher after-work hour visitor ratios are associated with increased aggravated assault and robbery frequency, likely due to more offenders and targets converging in these areas. Conversely, work hour visitor ratios show a stronger link to motor vehicle theft, suggesting that reduced guardianship during work hours may heighten crime opportunities. The relationships between visitor ratios and crime vary by crime type, indicating that temporal shifts in guardianship and offender-target interactions significantly influence urban crime patterns. These findings provide novel insights into the stability of crime patterns and the role of visitor dynamics, enriching the routine activity theory literature and offering implications for targeted crime prevention strategies in policing and urban planning.

title: High-harmonic generation during ultrafast melting of a Mott insulating state
abstractText: Abstract Solids in an intense laser field show high-harmonic generation (HHG), which can provide information on carrier dynamics and band structures in weakly correlated systems. In strongly correlated systems, a laser field can induce a transition between the various electronic phases formed by the entanglement of charge, spin, and orbital degrees of freedom via carrier generation. The HHG accompanying this process should contain information on the nonequilibrium electronic-state dynamics along the oscillating field—an aspect that remains unresolved to date. Here, we show that an intense mid-infrared (MIR) pulse induces a Mott insulator–metal transition in a one-dimensional cuprate, Sr2CuO3, the evolution of which is reflected by the spectral features of HHs. When the electric-field amplitude exceeds 6 MV/cm, carriers are efficiently generated and each harmonic frequency decreases from odd multiples of the MIR frequency. Dynamical mean-field theory indicates that these redshifts originate from a series of electronic-structure reconstructions in each electric-field cycle during the melting of the Mott-insulator state, which modifies the radiation phase from carrier recombination cycle-by-cycle. This phenomenon is negligible in rigid-band systems. This experimental-theoretical study confirms that HH spectroscopy research can potentially unravel the sub-cycle dynamics of nonequilibrium phase transitions in correlated materials.

title: Fault-tolerant quantum computing with high-rate symplectic double codes
abstractText: High-rate and large-distance quantum codes are expected to make fault-tolerant quantum computing more efficient, but most of them lack efficient fault-tolerant encoded-state preparation methods. We propose such fault-tolerant encoders for two symplectic double codes, [[30,6,5]] and [[36,12,5]]. The advantage of these codes is their compactness, namely, their small code block sizes for their high encoding rates and large distance, allowing for early experimental realization of high-rate codes. Detecting crucial errors during encoding with as few auxiliary qubits as possible, our encoders can reduce resource overheads while keeping low logical error rates compared to more naive methods. Numerical simulations with a circuit-level noise model demonstrate the reliability and effectiveness of the proposed methods. We also develop arbitrary-state encoders that enable the injection of arbitrary quantum states into the code spaces. Combined with basic fault-tolerant operations, they support universal quantum computation. We thus demonstrate that efficient and reliable logical state preparation is achievable even for compact and high-rate codes, offering a potential step toward efficient fault-tolerant quantum computing suitable for near-term experiments.

title: Selecting feeding behavior would enhance feed efficiency in slow-growing free-range broiler
abstractText: Abstract Background In the free-range poultry industry, commercial birds have access to outdoor environments where climatic conditions are variable and uncontrolled. However, breeding animals must be selected under confined and controlled conditions for sanitary reasons. These environmental differences can reduce selection efficiency due to genotype-by-environment (G×E) interactions, particularly affecting feed efficiency—a key trait for sustainability that impacts both economic performance and environmental footprint. Therefore, selection based solely on performance in confined conditions may not be optimal for free-range systems. To enhance sustainability in such systems, it is important to identify indoor traits genetically correlated with outdoor feed conversion ratios. This study investigates the potential for integrating feeding behavior traits into selection schemes for slow-growing broiler chickens raised outdoors during summer. Results We analyzed various feeding behaviors expressed indoors, including the number of meals, the timing and distribution of intake, and their variability both within and across days, as well as the correlation between these feeding behaviors and temperature. Many traits exhibited moderate to high heritability and were genetically correlated with outdoor feed conversion ratios. However, the correlations between traits were not always favorable: some behavioral traits were positively correlated with feed conversion ratio but they were negatively correlated with each other. To address these interactions, we summarized the G matrix of genetic variances and covariances among traits by its first two eigen vectors, g max and g 2 , accounting for 74% of the genetic variance in feeding behaviors. The g max axis included meal frequency, day-to-day variation in early-day intake, and meal number, while g 2 axis was mainly correlated with traits related to early-day feeding behaviors and their variation. Selection on the gmax axis could enhance feed efficiency and meat quality without compromising carcass yield, unlike selection on g 2 , which would improve feed efficiency at the expense of meat quality and carcass composition. Conclusions These findings suggest that incorporating feeding behavior traits, particularly those aligned with gmax, into indoor selection schemes could contribute to enhancing feed efficiency in outdoor environments.

title: A General Carathéodory Existence and Uniqueness Theorem for Fractional Differential Equations and an Application to Kinetic Models
abstractText: ABSTRACT In this paper, we establish a general version of Carathéodory's existence and uniqueness theorem for semilinear systems of integro‐differential equations driven by Caputo fractional derivatives of distinct orders. Our proof shows that the integrability exponent of the Carathéodory function must be strictly greater than the maximum of the reciprocals of the fractional orders in the system; otherwise, even the existence of a solution cannot be guaranteed. Our approach combines fine regularity estimates with delicate fractional integral techniques, offering new insights into the interplay between fractional differentiability and nonlinear dynamics in systems with mixed derivative orders. As an illustration, we apply our theorem to a two‐component kinetic model with distinct memory effects, obtaining a complete well‐posedness theory in a regime where classical continuity assumptions fail.

title: Sublevel-selective electron spin hyperpolarization of triplet radical pairs in metal–organic frameworks
abstractText: Molecular spin systems are promising platforms for spin-based technologies because their electronic structures can be synthetically tailored and integrated into higher-order assemblies. Photogenerated radical pairs can exhibit spin hyperpolarization under ambient conditions, yet extending such spin dynamics from isolated molecules to structurally organized materials remains challenging. Here, we report a metal–organic framework that regulates the generation of spin-polarized radical pairs within locally well-defined donor–acceptor arrangements. N,N’-di(4-pyridyl)−1,4,5,8-naphthalenetetracarboxdiimide is introduced into a zinc tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin-based framework. Dense donor–acceptor packing promotes efficient quenching of the porphyrin singlet excited state and selectively forms strongly coupled triplet radical pairs polarized in the zero-spin projection sublevel. These radical pairs exhibit narrow electron paramagnetic resonance signals and long spin-lattice relaxation times. Their spin-lattice relaxation dynamics persist in various guest solvents and vary with guest identity, demonstrating a route to chemically responsive spin materials based on porous, locally organized donor–acceptor frameworks. While molecular spin systems are promising platforms for spin-based technologies, previous studies have mainly focused on isolated molecular systems embedded in dense solid matrices. Here, the authors report a metal-organic framework approach for regulating the generation of spin-polarized radical pairs within a well-defined donor-acceptor arrangement.
