title: Ground state and excitations of quasiperiodic one-dimensional narrow-band moiré systems: A mean-field approach
abstractText: We demonstrate that a mean field approximation can be confidently employed in quasiperiodic moiré systems to treat interactions and quasiperiodicity on equal footing. We obtain the mean field phase diagram for an illustrative one-dimensional moiré system that exhibits narrow bands and a regime with non-interacting multifractal critical states. By systematically comparing our findings with existing exact results, we identify the regimes where the mean field approximation provides an accurate description. Interestingly, in the critical regime, we obtain a quasifractal charge density wave, consistent with the exact results. To complement this study, we employ a real-space implementation of the time-dependent Hartree-Fock, enabling the computation of the excitation spectrum and response functions at the RPA level. These findings indicate that a mean field approximation to treat systems hosting multifractal critical states, as found in two-dimensional quasiperiodic moiré systems, is an appropriate methodology.

title: Digital twins for intelligent intersections: A literature review
abstractText: Intelligent intersections play a pivotal role in urban mobility, demanding innovative solutions such as digital twins to enhance safety and efficiency. This literature review investigates the integration and application of digital twins for intelligent intersections, a critical area within smart urban traffic systems. The review systematically categorizes existing research into five key thematic areas: (i) Digital Twin Architectures and Frameworks; (ii) Data Processing and Simulation Techniques; (iii) Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Adaptive Traffic Control; (iv) Safety and Protection of Vulnerable Road Users; and (v) Scaling from Localized Intersections to Citywide Traffic Networks. Each theme is explored comprehensively, highlighting significant advancements, current challenges, and critical insights. The findings reveal that multi-layered digital twin architectures incorporating real-time data fusion and AI-driven decision-making enhances traffic efficiency and safety. Advanced simulation techniques combined with sophisticated AI/ML algorithms demonstrate notable improvements in real-time responsiveness and predictive accuracy for traffic management. Additionally, the integration of digital twins has shown substantial promise in safeguarding vulnerable road users through proactive and adaptive safety strategies. Despite these advancements, key challenges persist, including interoperability of diverse data sources, scalability of digital twins for extensive traffic networks, and managing uncertainty within dynamic urban environments. Addressing these challenges will be essential for the future development and deployment of intelligent, adaptive, and sustainable intersection management systems.

title: Primordial quark stars made of a long-lived false vacuum
abstractText: A false vacuum could be a profound ingredient of fundamental physics, yet its direct detection in laboratories is hindered when the lifetime is exponentially long. Conventional static phase diagrams often discard metastable false vacuum, we show that, however, in a dynamical treatment of a first-order QCD phase transition at large quark chemical potential that strongly suppresses tunneling, cosmologically long-lived, and thus indispensable false vacuum naturally arises, and makes nontrivial contribution to constituting primordial quark objects. We identify two distinct branches of such primordial quark objects: quark star crusted with false vacuum, and nugget specifically referring to quark star in global false vacuum, which may account for a population of small compact stars. Some long-lived primordial objects may have survived until the late Universe, and hopefully sow the seeds of high red-shift galaxies. Its false vacuum decay can power ultra-energetic long $γ$-ray bursts and kHz gravitational waves within multi-messenger facilities, rendering itself an astrophysical and thus testable phenomenon.

title: Rosette formations as symmetry breaking events
abstractText: Multicellular rosettes are observed in different situations such as morphogenesis, wound healing, and cancer progression. While some molecular insights have been gained to explain the presence of these assemblies of five or more cells around a common center, what are the tunable, global features that favors/hinders their formation is still largely unknown. Here, we made use of a Voronoi dynamical model to investigate the ingredients driving the emergence of rosettes characterized by different degree of stability and organization. We found that (i) breaking the local spatial symmetry of the system, i.e., introducing curvature-inducing defects, allows for the formation of rosette-like structures (ii) whose probability of formation depends on the characteristic of the cellular layer. In particular, a trade-off between tissue fluidity and single cell deformability dictates the assembly of transient rosettes, that are strongly stabilized in the presence of cell alignment interactions. To test our model predictions, we performed fluorescence microscopy experiments on rosette-forming neural populations derived from induced pluripotent stem cells, finding significant agreement. Overall, our work may set the stage to gain an unifying understanding of the plethora of biophysical mechanisms involving the occurrence of rosette-like structure both in physiology and their altered formation in pathology.

title: Immersive and wearable bi-directional thermal rendering for physical and virtual interaction in augmented reality
abstractText: Augmented reality blends virtual content with the physical world, creating a challenge for thermal feedback: users must feel virtual temperature cues without losing dexterity or access to real-world thermal information. Here we show that a palm-mounted warm/cool thermal feedback prototype can address this challenge through three design considerations: indirect feedback that leaves the fingertips unobstructed, active thermal passthrough that senses and reproduces the temperature of contacted physical surfaces, and spatially and temporally varying thermal stimulation. Human-subject experiments show that indirect feedback preserves immersion and comfort despite reduced realism when visual contact occurs at the fingertips; thermal passthrough supports discrimination between real and rendered temperatures; and moving thermal patterns increase immersion and realism compared with static stimulation. These findings suggest that our design considerations are viable design strategies for AR thermal haptics, while also clarifying tradeoffs for applications that require precise realism versus broader immersive thermal experience.

title: End milling tool condition monitoring with vibration signals and machine learning classifiers: a comparative study
abstractText: Abstract Contemporary industrial businesses are encountering issues related to tool wear. To address this issue, the implementation of tool condition monitoring (TCM) is imperative, necessitating the development of such solutions. These technologies will help improve the tool's product quality and life and ultimately reduce the tool wear. The present article focuses on multipoint milling tool supervision (Health Monitoring of End Milling Tool) using a Machine Learning approach. In this experimentation, vibration signature data has collected for the multipoint milling tool, extracted vibration signatures (signals) have further used for statistical feature extraction. The J48 algorithm's decision tree have taken to select the best features. The fault classification has carried with a different classifier such as Logit Boost, linear regression, Simple Logistic, and Bagged trees classifier. Comparison of these classifiers is carried out based on vibration signatures, and out of these classifiers, the Logit Boost classifier gives better classification and accuracy than other classifiers. In the Logit Boost, linear regression, Simple Logistic, and Bagged trees classifier, maximum classification accuracy was 95.83%, 95%, 94.38%, and 94.54%, respectively, with a selection of the best statistical features. Similarly, classification accuracy was 96.25%, 95.2083%, 93.75%, and 92.7083% without selecting the best features. The wavelet analysis has been used to compare maximum classification accuracy with statistical feature extraction.In this Daubechies, Symlets, Haar and Discrete Meyer wavelet, Coiflet wavelet family classification accuracy have obtained. In the Daubechies wavelet family, utmost classification accuracy is 99.38% with db5 wavelet, and in the symlets wavelet family, utmost classification accuracy has received with a simple logistic classifier, i.e., 99.17% with sym5 wavelet.

title: Measurements, simulations, and models of the point-spread function of electron-beam lithography
abstractText: Abstract When a sample is exposed using electron-beam lithography, the electrons scatter deep and far in the substrate, resulting in unwanted deposition of dose at both the nano- and the microscale. This proximity effect can be mitigated by proximity effect correction provided that accurate and validated models of the point-spread function of the electron scattering are available. Most works so far considered a double-Gaussian model of the electron point-spread function, which is very inaccurate for modern electron-beam writers with high acceleration voltages. We present measurements of the process point-spread function for chemically semi-amplified resist on silicon and indium phosphide substrates using a 150 kV electron-beam lithography system. We find that the double-Gaussian model deviates from experiments by up to four orders of magnitude. We propose instead a model comprising the sum of a power-law and a Gaussian, which is in excellent agreement with simulations of the electron scattering obtained by a Monte Carlo method. We apply the power-law plus Gaussian model to quantify the electron scattering and proximity effect correction parameters across material stacks, processing, and voltages from 5 kV to 150 kV. We find that the power-law term remains remarkably constant, whereas the long-range dose contributions and the clearing dose are significantly affected by the substrate and the acceleration voltage. Combined, the results imply that reliance on the double-Gaussian approximation in proximity-effect correction has become a limiting factor for resolution in fabrication at the nanoscale.

Zusammenhänge zwischen den Bayley Scales III und dem Beobachtungsverfahren MONDEY: Eine Validitätsanalyse
abstractText: Zusammenfassung: Theoretischer Hintergrund: Alltagsnahe Entwicklungsdiagnostik durch Beobachtung kann eine wichtige Ergänzung zu standardisierten Entwicklungstest darstellen. Fragestellung: Die vorliegende Arbeit untersucht Zusammenhänge zwischen dem standardisierten Entwicklungstest Bayley-III und dem Beobachtungsinstrument MONDEY hinsichtlich konvergenter Validität. Der Fokus liegt auf den Entwicklungsbereichen Denken und Sprache bei Kindern im Alter von 21 ( n1 = 33, w = 14) und 26 ( n2 = 30, w = 15) Monaten. Methode: Die elterlichen Einschätzungen der Entwicklung wurden mittels MONDEY erhoben und mit den standardisierten Testergebnissen der Bayley-III in Zusammenhang gesetzt. Die Übereinstimmung der Beurteilungen innerhalb der Entwicklungsbereiche wurden korrelativ untersucht. Zusätzlich wurden explorative Analysen zu korrelativen Zusammenhängen über Entwicklungsbereiche hinweg durchgeführt. Ergebnisse: Die Ergebnisse zeigen hohe Korrelationen zwischen den Sprachskalen ( r = .75, p < .001) sowie moderate Zusammenhänge zwischen den Kognitionsskalen ( r = .50, p < .001) beider Instrumente. Die Skaleninterkorrelationen fallen bei den Bayley-III höher als in MONDEY raus. Diskussion und Schlussfolgerung: Die Befunde unterstützen die Annahme, dass MONDEY eine valide Ergänzung zur standardisierten Entwicklungsdiagnostik darstellen kann. Zudem scheint die Trennschärfe der MONDEY-Skalen für die Bereiche Kognition und Sprache höher zu sein als die der Bayley-III. Somit lassen sich Hinweise auf konvergente, aber auch diskriminante Validität der Instrumente finden.

title: Holographic Schwinger effect with translational symmetry breaking
abstractText: Abstract We investigate the holographic Schwinger effect in a background with translational symmetry breaking (TSB) at finite chemical potential. The gravitational background is characterized by two independent parameters: the TSB parameter $$\alpha $$ α , which controls momentum relaxation, and the chemical potential $$\mu $$ μ , which determines the finite density of the dual field theory. Using the potential analysis method, we derive the total potential governing the pair production process and examine its dependence on $$\alpha $$ α , $$\mu $$ μ , the external magnetic field, and the ratio $$\beta =E/E_c$$ β = E / E c . Our results show that the effects of $$\alpha $$ α and $$\mu $$ μ on the Schwinger process strongly depend on the dynamical regime. In the subcritical regime, increasing either $$\alpha $$ α or $$\mu $$ μ lowers the potential barrier and facilitates pair production. However, near and above the critical electric field, the roles of these two parameters become qualitatively different. While increasing the chemical potential lowers the total potential and enhances the Schwinger pair production process, increasing the translational symmetry breaking parameter shifts the potential upward and suppresses the production process. We further show that, at fixed $$\beta =E/E_c$$ β = E / E c , a perpendicular external magnetic field lowers the effective potential barrier and thereby facilitates the Schwinger process, while the physical electric field changes accordingly through the magnetic-field dependence of $$E_c$$ E c . The corresponding pair production rate is not independently calculated; instead, its qualitative behavior is characterized through a proxy derived from the total potential. Overall, our analysis provides a comprehensive picture of how translational symmetry breaking, finite density, and external magnetic fields influence holographic non-perturbative pair production.

title: Direct signatures of Anderson orthogonality catastrophe in nonequilibrium quantum dots
abstractText: We propose schemes for unambiguous direct observation of Anderson orthogonality catastrophe (AOC) effects in a quantum dot coupled to a charge detector, enabling experimental estimation of the AOC exponent $α$. We show that certain easy-to-measure observables have a robust dependence on $α$ in the non-equilibrium regimes of source-drain voltage bias or thermal imbalance. Our results are obtained using a rate equation formalism in which the AOC effects on tunnel rates are incorporated in an exact manner, and directly support recent experimental results.

title: Intra-annual grounding-line migration and retreat: insights from high-resolution satellite and in situ observations over Milne Glacier in the Canadian High Arctic
abstractText: Monitoring changes in the position of the boundary where marine-terminating glaciers transition from grounded to floating, known as the grounding line, is critical for advancing our understanding of glacier stability. The grounding line is difficult to observe directly but can be inferred from the ice surface tidal-flexure zone. This zone spans from the inland limit of tidal flexure – the hinge line, across the grounding line to the hydrostatic line, where the glacier becomes freely floating. We explore flexure-zone changes on Milne Glacier, Nunavut, Canada from 2023 to 2024 at a high spatial resolution of 10 m using 4 d RADARSAT Constellation Mission (RCM) data acquisitions from four different orbits. The Double Difference Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (DDInSAR) technique was employed to delineate 116 flexure zones through time, which were then examined with respect to SAR viewing geometry, tides and atmospheric pressure variability, glacier velocity changes, and ice bending, as well as ice surface and bed topography. The most reliable flexure-zone delineation (horizontal uncertainty of ±8 m) was achieved with ascending RCM tracks at low incidence angles during periods when the ice velocity was steady and bending was not substantial, resulting in a combined SAR line-of-sight error of 0.13 cm. A worst-case flexure-zone delineation uncertainty of ±222 m was noted when a descending track with a high incidence angle was used and glacier velocity became more variable, increasing the combined SAR line-of-sight error to 3.26 cm. Low-error DDInSAR images enabled the detection of a newly developed ∼2.4 km grounding-line retreat associated with the emergence of a new pinning point at the eastern margin of the glacier. Our results underscore that care must be taken to ensure that the low-error DDInSAR results are used when monitoring changes in grounding-line position and that pinning points alter the grounding-line short-term migration and its long-term retreat.

title: TaxoAttention: fusing semantic and hierarchical taxonomic models with attention-guided augmentation for mosquito identification
abstractText: Accurate species-level identification of mosquitoes remains a critical bottleneck in vector surveillance, particularly when dealing with morphologically similar taxa or field-damaged specimens. In this study, we introduce a deep learning framework that integrates hierarchical taxonomic structure with attention-based feature learning to improve classification performance under real-world imaging conditions. The model combines a semi-fixed, taxonomy-informed feature stream with a fully trainable semantic stream. It further employs dynamic attention-guided augmentation, designed to focus training on diagnostically relevant regions, such as wing venation, tarsal banding, and palpal morphology, and to reduce the influence of the background. Evaluated on a standardized, predominantly field-collected dataset (MosquitoTax-200) representing 32 species across Aedes, Anopheles, and Culex with 200 images per species, our approach achieves 84.6% macro-averaged precision (mAP), 5.0 percentage points above an Xception baseline trained with standard cross-entropy loss and used as a control. This work highlights the potential of biologically grounded AI tools to scale species identification in vector control operations and to support training and quality assurance in entomological diagnostics.

title: Certainties and Sensitivity Analysis of the Global Economy: A GDP by End-Use Approach
abstractText: This research first analyses the evolution of four GDP by end-use variables (Household Consumption, Government Spending, Exports, and Imports) for the top 40 economies in the world, covering up to 90% of the global economy. The first part of the research project is determined by a longitudinal analysis of 40+ years, resulting in a linear regression to the expected GDP value of each nation for 2030. Secondly, both a Monte Carlo and a sensitivity simulation analysis are performed. The analysis reveals that the most sensitive variables that contribute to the dispersion of the GDP by end-use future results are imports, followed by exports. Also, Household Consumption appears with a small presence, while the Government Spending factor shows no sensitivity in the model. This research demonstrates the crucial importance of adjusting the balance of trade.

title: Protocol for generating parasympathetic neurons from hiPSCs and their coculture with hiPSC-atrial cardiomyocytes
abstractText: Summary Peripheral parasympathetic ganglia lie adjacent to their target organs; their dysfunction contributes to diseases like atrial fibrillation. Due to their challenging accessibility for primary culture, we provide a step-by-step protocol to generate parasympathetic neurons from human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSC). They reproduce numerous native physiological features: cholinergic and autonomic markers, functional nicotinic receptors and electrophysiological properties. We also describe a co-culture system with hiPSC-atrial cardiomyocytes allowing neuromodulation of cardiomyocyte activity and offering a platform for drug discovery and disease modelling. title: Reconstructing rangeland soil carbon erosion using sediment trapped behind small reservoir dams
abstractText: Human-induced soil erosion significantly impacts soil organic carbon (SOC) dynamics, particularly in rangelands, where land degradation and overgrazing exacerbate SOC loss. This study investigates whether sediments from small farm reservoirs in South Africa's Karoo rangelands can serve as archives to reconstruct the temporal pattern of SOC changes during the 20th-century. Sediments from three dams, accumulated during different time periods, were analysed for radionuclide markers (e.g. 137Cs), organic carbon (OC) content, sediment yield and OC flux. The results illustrate the suitability of the farm dam sediments to reconstruct soil erosion history in the Karoo and reveal distinct temporal patterns of SOC erosion for each catchment. For all dams, increases in sediment input into the reservoirs did not correspond to a proportional increase in organic carbon accumulation, highlighting the influence of land degradation on SOC depletion over time. Dam-specific variations underscore the role of land use and local heterogeneity in shaping erosion and carbon fluxes. These findings suggest that lateral SOC transfer has been dynamic during the 20th century, challenging models that assume constant sediment OC concentrations over time. Therefore, this study illustrates the importance of reconstructing past SOC dynamics and gain a correct understanding of the carbon fluxes in degraded rangelands and their broader implications for the global carbon cycle during the 20th century.

title: Lynx reintroduction from a bottlenecked source exposes a lethal genetic defect
abstractText: Abstract Conservation programmes worldwide use reintroductions and translocations as management tools to support endangered species. However, such efforts often result in small and isolated populations that face genetic challenges associated with reduced gene flow and inbreeding. Inbreeding depression is a well-known risk in such programmes, as increased homozygosity can expose recessive deleterious alleles, compromise fitness and threaten population persistence. Yet, no causal variant for a lethal disease has previously been identified in a wild population. Here we combine long-term health and population data with genomic analyses to identify a recessive loss-of-function allele causing lethal organ mineralization in young Eurasian lynx ( Lynx lynx ) from a reintroduced population in Switzerland. Spatio-temporal analyses revealed that the allele was introduced from one of the source populations and increased in frequency through founder effects and inbreeding. Our findings establish the first direct link between reintroduction history and a lethal genetic disease in the wild, illustrating how population genetic processes interact to shape the fate of a recessive deleterious allele and emphasize the vulnerability of small, isolated populations following reintroduction.

title: The Ingleton inequality holds for metacyclic groups and fails for supersoluble groups
abstractText: Abstract The Ingleton inequality first appeared in matroid theory, where Ingleton proved in 1971 that every rank function coming from a representable matroid on four subsets satisfies a particular inequality. Because this inequality is not implied by submodularity, Shannon-type axioms alone, it and various analogues play a central role in separately linear and non-linear phenomena in a variety of areas of mathematics. The Ingleton inequality for finite groups concerns the various intersections of four subgroups. It holds for many quadruples of subgroups of finite groups, but not all, the smallest example being four subgroups of $$S_5,$$ S 5 , of order 120. Open questions are whether the Ingleton inequality always holds for metacyclic and nilpotent groups. (There is a proof in the literature due to Oggier and Stancu, but there is an already known issue with their proof, which we address in this article.) In this paper, we prove that the Ingleton inequality always holds for metacyclic groups, but that it fails for supersoluble groups, a class of groups only a little larger than nilpotent groups. Although we do not resolve the nilpotent case here, we do make some reductions, and also prove that there are no nilpotent violators of the Ingleton inequality of order less than 1024. We end with a list of Ingleton inequality violating groups of order at most 1023. The article comes with a Magma package that allows reproduction of all results in the paper and for the reader to check the Ingleton inequality for any given finite group.

title: Agreement of an invasive angiography-derived computational model of coronary microvascular physiology against continuous thermodilution
abstractText: Coronary microvascular dysfunction is associated with myocardial ischaemia and an adverse prognosis, but accurate invasive assessment is technically challenging, requires dedicated hardware and increases procedure time and cost. Assessment can be performed with three-dimensional (3D) computational fluid dynamics (CFD) modelling, but this technique lacks robust in vivo validation. In this study, we compared the accuracy of a 3D CFD method against continuous thermodilution (CIT). Patients with acute and chronic coronary syndromes, undergoing CIT and angiography-derived assessment, were prospectively recruited from two tertiary cardiac centres. Invasive coronary angiographic images were used to reconstruct 3D anatomy in silico . Microvascular resistance reserve (MRR) and absolute flow were computed using 3D CFD in reconstructed coronary arteries. Invasive pressure measurements, recorded during fractional flow reserve assessment, informed the CFD boundary conditions. Paired flow results were available for 131 arteries from 89 patients. Median FFR was 0.81 [0.70 – 0.89] and 108 (81%) vessels contained an epicardial stenosis. Median computed MRR was 2.31 [1.83 – 3.00], which was significantly lower than CIT assessed MRR (2.79 [2.21 – 3.52], z = 3.57, p = 0.0004). There was evidence of a moderate relationship between computed and measured MRR (ρ = 0.58, p < 0.0001) and area under the receiver operator characteristic curve was 0.77 (95% CI 0.68–0.86), indicating fair classification. There was a moderate relationship between computed and measured hyperaemic vessel inlet flow (ρ = 0.44, p < 0.0001). For both MRR and flow, agreement improved at lower, more clinically relevant, values. In this clinical validation study, when compared with CIT, the novel CFD method demonstrated a moderate correlation, and fair diagnostic accuracy. This CFD method may be a useful, low-cost and less-invasive tool in the assessment of microvascular physiology that could complement current invasive techniques.

title: Prediction of lncRNA-protein interacting pairs using LLM embeddings based on evolutionary information
abstractText: Interactions of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) with proteins is responsible for numerous cellular processes, including transcriptional regulation, chromatin remodeling, cell differentiation, and intracellular signaling. Several computational methods have been developed for predicting lncRNA–protein interaction (LPI) pairs; however, many existing approaches were developed using earlier versions of interaction databases, potentially limiting their applicability to more recently characterized interactions. In this study, we developed a sequence-based framework for LPI prediction using a large non-redundant dataset comprising 128,374 interacting and an equal number of non-interacting pairs. Initially, similarity-based approach BLAST was tried which had poor discriminative power, due to low sequence similarity between sequences. Subsequently, we developed convolutional neural network and machine learning models using sequence-derived features and protein language model embeddings. The CatBoost model integrating Dinucleotide Autocorrelation (DACC) features for lncRNAs and ESM-2-t30 embeddings for proteins achieved an AUC of 0.929 on the training dataset and 0.692 on the homology-aware validation dataset. These results demonstrate the potential of combining sequence-derived features and protein language model representations for LPI prediction while highlighting the challenges associated with generalization to sequences with limited homology to the training data. We developed standalone software and web server lncrnaPI for predicting LPI pairs, scanning lncRNA interacting proteins in proteome and protein interacting lncRNA in genomes ( https://webs.iiitd.edu.in/raghava/lncrnapi/ ).

title: Effect of ionizing photon escape fraction in faint galaxies on modeling reionization history of the universe
abstractText: We present model calculations of the reionization history of hydrogen using star formation histories, computed with a galaxy formation model which reproduces properties of local dwarf galaxies and UV luminosity functions of galaxies at z = 5 − 16 . We use the ionizing photon density functions predicted by the model along with different models for the escape fraction of ionizing photons, , to study the effects of ionizing photons from faint galaxies and different assumptions about on the evolution of hydrogen ionized fraction with redshift, . We show that accounting for the contribution of faint galaxies with UV luminosities M 1500 > − 13 , and with a {} ionizing photon escape fraction of results in the hydrogen reionization history consistent with all current observational constraints. Comparing results of the model and two alternative models shows that the model with a strong luminosity dependence of , which assigns high to faint galaxies, results in early reionization inconsistent with observational constraints. However, the model in which follows a universal redshift-independent correlation with the recent maximum specific star formation rate, motivated by the results of the SPHINX galaxy formation simulation, results in the reionization history in good agreement with existing observational constraints, even though this model produces a sizeable ionized hydrogen fraction of at redshifts z = 8 − 12 . Our results show that the relative contribution of faint dwarf galaxies to reionization depends sensitively on assumptions about the escape fraction for galaxies of different luminosities, and that this is the main source of uncertainty in modeling hydrogen reionization.

title: Concentrated sets and the Hurewicz property
abstractText: Abstract A set of reals X is $$\mathfrak {b}$$ b -concentrated if it has cardinality at least $$\mathfrak {b}$$ b and it contains a countable set $$D\subseteq X$$ D ⊆ X such that each closed subset of X disjoint from D has size smaller than $$\mathfrak {b}$$ b . We present ZFC results about structures of $$\mathfrak {b}$$ b -concentrated sets with the Hurewicz covering property using semifilters. Then we show that assuming that the semifilter trichotomy holds each $$\mathfrak {b}$$ b -concentrated set is Hurewicz and even productively Hurewicz. We also show that the appearance of Hurewicz $$\mathfrak {b}$$ b -concentrated sets under the semifilter trichotomy is somewhat specific and the situation in the Laver model for the consistency of the Borel Conjecture is different.

title: Emergent long-tailed dynamics in spin ice
abstractText: In this study, we reveal long-tail dynamics spontaneously arising from a magnetic system. Specifically, we consider a classical spin system and demonstrate the emergence of a spin-ice physics when drive-induced heating is well suppressed. We show that at high driving frequencies, magnetic monopole excitations exhibit nonergodic stochastic dynamics characterized by power-law-distributed trapping times with long tails—a behavior that persists even in the absence of driving. At intermediate driving frequencies, the system eventually heats up to an infinite-temperature state. However, contrary to conventional wisdom of Floquet heating, the heating time in our model is extremely sensitive to different initial-state realizations and also follows a long-tailed power-law distribution, which arise specifically due to periodic driving. We show that an effective short-range attractive interaction between monopoles is responsible for the long-tailed distributions observed in both monopole and heating dynamics.

title: Weakly Centered Weighted Composition Operators in $$L^2$$-spaces
abstractText: Weakly centered and spectrally weakly centered weighted composition operators in $$L^2$$ -spaces are characterized. Sufficient conditions for existence of invariant subspaces are given. Additional results and examples are supplied.

title: Elliptic systems generating a positive semigroup are decoupled
abstractText: Abstract We show that the semigroup associated to a second-order elliptic system is positive if and only if the differential equations are essentially decoupled and the coefficients are real-valued. This means the system can be replaced by an equivalent decoupled system (which defines the same semigroup). Instead of matrix coefficients we more generally consider operator-valued coefficients, which leads to interesting additional difficulties with respect to Banach space valued integration.

title: Sequence-Driven Classification of Aptamers by Target Type: Algorithm Development and Validation
abstractText: Abstract Background DNA aptamers are short, single-stranded oligonucleotides that bind molecular targets with high affinity and specificity. Traditionally, aptamers are identified through SELEX (systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment), an iterative process that is time-consuming and requires specialized equipment. To simplify and accelerate aptamer discovery, particularly across multiple molecular targets, computational approaches have gained momentum. Objective In this study, we present a sequence-only framework for classifying DNA aptamers by target type using curated datasets of experimentally validated sequences. Target type here refers to the broad class of ligands that an aptamer binds to. Methods Aptamer-target records were curated from the UTexas Aptamer Database, retaining only those sequences with complete annotations and a clearly defined target category. From these filtered records, the 2 target categories with the highest number of unique aptamer sequences—cell and steroid, comprising a total of 236 sequences—were selected for this study. Each sequence was then represented using character-level term frequency–inverse document frequency of n-gram motifs (n=3‐6) combined with guanine-cytosine content and sequence length. The dataset was then split into 70% training, 20% testing, and 10% validation sets. An ensemble of 9 bagged extreme gradient boosting classifiers was selected for its established performance on high-dimensional tabular data and native handling of class imbalance. The model was trained to distinguish between aptamers targeting cellular and steroidal molecules, with class weighting, oversampling, probability calibration, and per-class threshold optimization applied to address class imbalance. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, macro- F 1 scores, and recall on the test dataset and an independently generated external validation set comprising 13 new laboratory-generated steroid (aldosterone)–binding aptamers. The novelty of these laboratory aptamers relative to the training set was also confirmed using the pairwise Levenshtein distance. Results The ensemble classifier achieved 97.92% accuracy and a macro- F 1 -score of 0.95 on a test set of 236 curated DNA aptamer sequences, demonstrating strong performance in distinguishing cell-binding from steroid-binding aptamers. The calibrated and threshold-optimized model was further validated on a set of 13 new laboratory-created aptamers for steroid aldosterone using experimental SELEX, achieving 100% recall and confirming its ability to generalize to new experimental data. Conclusions These results demonstrate that informative, target-specific patterns can be directly extracted from DNA sequences, establishing a scalable, data-driven complement to SELEX in this preliminary proof-of-concept study for rapid prescreening of candidate aptamers. More broadly, this sequence-only approach could support faster, lower-cost triage of candidate aptamers, reducing reliance on iterative wet-laboratory SELEX as aptamer databases and target categories continue to expand.

title: Deciphering the global genomic landscape of C. neoformans: population dynamics, molecular epidemiology and genomic signatures of pathogenicity
abstractText: Abstract Background Cryptococcus neoformans is an opportunistic fungal pathogen that exhibits extensive ecological resilience and is a leading cause of fungal meningitis. Despite its clinical significance, the global population structure, evolutionary dynamics, virulence-associated genome architecture, and antifungal resistance landscape remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the global genomic diversity, molecular epidemiology, phylogenetic relationships, virulome, and resistome of C. neoformans using an integrated comparative genomic approach. Methods In total, we analyzed 139 C. neoformans genomes, comprising 138 publicly available genomes and one laboratory isolate from India. The molecular epidemiological characteristics were analyzed by serotype, molecular type, sequence type and mating type. We performed comparative genomic analyzes to investigate genome-wide similarity, phylogenetic relations and pangenome architecture. The virulome and resistome were characterized by systematic screening of virulence-associated genes and antifungal resistance-associated genes. Representative strains, H99 and Cn, were used to provide further preliminary phenotypic insights through in vitro antifungal susceptibility testing. Result The dataset comprised 126 clinical and 13 environmental isolates. Molecular epidemiological profiling showed a high prevalence of serotype A, molecular type VNI (88%), sequence type ST5 (63%) and mating type MATα (approximately 92%) indicating a highly conserved and largely clonal population structure. Southern Africa was identified as a key region of genomic diversity, with phylogenomic analysis revealing distinct evolutionary lineages, with VNB as the predominant variant among Southern African isolates. High average nucleotide identity (~99.9%) and a closed pangenome structure (Heap’s law exponent = 0.0005) further suggested extensive genomic conservation. Comparative analysis of 17 major virulence-associated genes showed that 11 were part of the core genome. Resistome profiling identified genetic differences in genes related to antifungal resistance, in particular ERG11 , FUR1 , FCY2 and MSH2 , with ERG11 I99V being the most frequent substitution found (56.8%). Conclusion These findings emphasize the worldwide dominance of a hyperclonal VNI-ST5-MATα lineage, a closed pangenome architecture and the conservation of major virulence and antifungal resistance-associated determinants in C. neoformans . This baseline study underscores the need for integrated clinical-genomic surveillance to track hyperclonal dissemination, conserved virulence, and adaptive resistance in this WHO critical-priority pathogen.

title: ProxSTORM—a stochastic trust-region algorithm for nonsmooth optimization
Adiabatic passage of 205 TlF with microwaves in a cryogenic beam
abstractText: We present a hyperfine-resolved state preparation scheme for thallium fluoride (TlF) molecules based on microwave-driven adiabatic passage (AP) in a spatially varying electric field. This method enables efficient and robust population transfer between selected $\left|J,m_J=0\right\rangle$ hyperfine sublevels of the $X\,^1Σ^+_0$ ground state in a cryogenic molecular beam, a key requirement for the CeNTREX search for nuclear time-reversal symmetry violation. Two sequential stages of AP are implemented. The first transfers population from $J=0$ to $J=1$ at a local field of $173~\mathrm{V/cm}$, and the second transfers from $J=1$ to $J=2$ at $110~\mathrm{V/cm}$. Transfer efficiencies are quantified through laser-induced fluorescence, and accounting for residual population in excited rotational levels after a prior stage of rotational cooling. We achieve state transfer efficiencies of $0.92(6)$ and $1.05(5)$ for the first and second states of AP, respectively. This corresponds to a total efficiency of $0.97(8)$ for population transfer from $J=0$ to $J=2$. These results demonstrate robust and high-fidelity preparation of specific rotational/hyperfine states in TlF.

title: Evolution of inhomogeneities in two-dimensional disordered superconductors in a magnetic field
abstractText: Emerging granularity in superconducting films by tuning disorder is a well-studied topic, both theoretically and experimentally. However, the orbital magnetic field generates a vortex lattice and contributes to the formation of periodic inhomogeneities. Here, we study superconducting films in the simultaneous presence of disorder and a magnetic field, examining how inhomogeneities in various superconducting correlations evolve under these two perturbations. By performing scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS) on thin films of \ce{Sr2VO_{3-\text{x}}FeAs} layer structures under both zero and finite orbital magnetic fields, we report impressive similarities between our theoretical results and the experimental findings. Our results have strong implications for identifying the nature of vortices in disordered superconductors, demonstrating a crossover from Abrikosov to Josephson character with increasing disorder, and provide predictive guidance for interpreting STS and current mapping data in complex superconductors.

title: Scaling and exceedance probability of sinkhole collapse in evaporite karst (Dead Sea, Jordan)
abstractText: Quantitative analysis of sinkhole collapse hazard requires robust data in both space and time. It also needs a clear understanding of the factors and processes that contribute to observed sinkhole locations and dimensions. In many karst settings, these criteria are difficult to meet because of the millennia-long time scales over which sinkhole populations are generated and because of uncertainties around how geomorphological processes link to sinkhole dimensions. This study presents new data on the scaling and probability of sinkhole formation in evaporite karst on the eastern Dead Sea shore (Jordan). Several thousand cover collapse sinkholes have formed there in the past 40 years with minimal post-collapse modification. Genetic processes and timescales are thus well constrained. Utilising high-resolution satellite imagery (Pleiades, PNEO) from 2017–2024, integrated with prior datasets, we present an updated inventory of sinkhole occurrence, extent and dimensions through time over the period 1992–2024. The sinkhole number increased by 43 % from 1565 in 2018 to 2247 in 2024, reflecting a 22 % increase in the sinkhole-affected land area to ca. 179 610 m 2 (17.9 ha). Formation of new karst subsidence features has continued a northward and seaward advance, consistent with control from the decline of the Dead Sea base level. However, we also observed a localised revival in 2021–2022 of sinkhole formation in an area that had been apparently inactive since 2002. This combination of continued and renewed sinkhole formation poses significant challenges to agriculture, housing and infrastructure in the area. Sinkhole average diameters range from 1.1 to 72.9 m; their frequency follows a log-normal distribution, rather than a power-law. Representative annualised exceedance probabilities for formation of sinkholes with diameters greater than 5, 10 and 50 m are ca. 70 %, 30 % and 0.5 % respectively. Exceedance probabilities show slight dependence on sampling time interval and on the nature of near-surface materials in which sinkholes form. Given their log-normal size distribution, the Dead Sea cover collapse sinkholes are not scale-free; instead they are scale-bound by the evaporite karst system's geometrical and mechanical properties.

title: A Decomposition-Based Robust Training of Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Nearly Incompressible Linear Elasticity
abstractText: Abstract. Due to divergence instability, the accuracy of low-order conforming finite element methods for nearly incompressible elasticity deteriorates as the Lamé coefficient [Formula: see text], or equivalently as the Poisson ratio [Formula: see text]. While this locking phenomenon is well known in classical numerical methods, its impact on physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) has not been systematically studied. We show that standard PINNs also suffer from a form of locking (PINN locking) in the nearly incompressible regime, leading to severe degradation in approximation quality and optimization performance. Our main contribution is a decomposition-based PINN formulation that rewrites the elasticity equations into balanced subsystems, yielding a PINN locking-robust training framework whose performance does not deteriorate with large [Formula: see text]. The framework applies to both forward and inverse problems and accommodates constant, variable, and parametric Lamé coefficients. We further perform a priori error analysis for the proposed formulation. Numerical experiments demonstrate consistent and substantial improvements over standard PINNs in both solution accuracy and parameter recovery across a wide range of nearly incompressible settings. title: The Synthetic Absorption Line Spectral Almanac (SALSA)
abstractText: We create the first large-scale mock spectroscopic survey of gas absorption sightlines traversing the interstellar medium (ISM), circumgalactic medium (CGM), and intergalactic medium (IGM) surrounding galaxies of virtual Universes. That is, we create mock, or synthetic, absorption spectra by drawing lines-of-sight through cosmological hydrodynamical simulations, using a new mesh-free Voronoi ray-tracing algorithm. The result is the Synthetic Absorption Line Spectral Almanac (SALSA), which is publicly released on a feature-rich online science platform (www.tng-project.org/spectra). It spans a range of ions, transitions, instruments, observational characteristics, assumptions, redshifts, and simulations. These include, but are not limited to: (ions) HI, OI, CI, MgI, MgII, FeII, SiII, CaII, ZnII, SiIII, SiIV, NV, CII, CIV, OVI; (instruments) SDSS-BOSS, KECK-HIRES, UVES, COS, DESI, 4MOST, WEAVE, XSHOOTER; (model choices) with/without dust depletion, noise, quasar continua, foregrounds; (redshift) from z=0 to z~6; (ancillary data) integrated equivalent widths, column densities, distances and properties of nearby galaxies; (simulations) IllustrisTNG including TNG50, TNG-Cluster, EAGLE, and SIMBA. We also provide line-of-sight integrals, including Faraday rotation measure (RM) probing magnetic fields, and dispersion measure (DM) as traced by fast radio bursts (FRBs). This scope is not fixed, and will grow and evolve with community interest and requests over time. The resulting dataset is generic and broadly applicable, enabling diverse science goals such as: (i) studies of the underlying physical gas structures giving rise to particular absorption signatures, (ii) galaxy-absorber and halo-absorber correlations, (iii) virtual surveys and survey strategy optimization, (iv) stacking experiments and the identification of faint absorption features, (v) assessment of data reduction methods and completeness calculations, (vi) inference of physical properties from observables, and (vii) apples-to-apples comparisons between simulations and data.

title: All-gaussian state discrimination beyond the coherent helstrom bound
abstractText: A core problem in communications is the optimal discrimination of binary-phase-shift-keyed (BPSK) signals. A longstanding goal has been to reach the fundamental quantum limit, known as the Helstrom bound, for BPSK signals encoded in coherent states. However, due to technical constraints, proposals for reaching the bound remain impractical. In this letter we take an alternative approach: using only Gaussian optics - displaced squeezed states and homodyne detection - we achieve discrimination of BPSK signals with error rates below what can be achieved using coherent states and any quantum measurement.

title: Making sense of quantum teleportation: an intervention study on students’ conceptions using a diagrammatic approach
abstractText: Abstract Quantum physics education at the upper-secondary level traditionally follows a historical approach, rarely extending beyond early 20th-century ideas, leaving students unprepared for comprehending modern quantum technologies central to everyday life and many facets of modern industry. To address this gap, we investigated how upper-secondary students and pre-service teachers understand quantum teleportation when taught with a simplified diagrammatic formalism based on the ZX-calculus, which represents quantum processes as diagrams of wires and boxes. Through phenomenographic analysis of video-recorded group work sessions, written responses to exercises, and a group interview, with a total of $n=21$ n = 21 participants, we identified an outcome space consisting of four qualitatively different, hierarchically ordered categories of description encapsulating the different ways of experiencing quantum teleportation. The categories revealed that a conceptual progression depends on how one understands the temporality in quantum processes, the role of entanglement in quantum teleportation, the active nature of quantum measurements, and interpretations of mathematical operations in the diagrams. Our findings indicate that while a simplified diagrammatic formalism for teaching quantum physics can provide an accessible entry point at the upper-secondary level, it does not automatically resolve fundamental conceptual challenges, and requires careful consideration in terms of developing teaching and learning sequences. Finally, these results provide educators with a deeper understanding of conceptual affordances and challenges for designing and improving instruction, while also highlighting the need for further exploring how students and teachers alike understand quantum phenomena.

title: One-sided witnesses for the quantumness of gravitational dynamics
abstractText: Quantum information concepts and quantum technologies have opened the prospect of probing the quantum nature of gravity in table-top experiments. Most proposals rely on detecting gravitationally mediated entanglement, which requires measurements on both interacting systems. Here we propose an alternative test based on witnessing quantum memory effects in the dynamics of a single system. We show how the quantum memory concept allows the non-classicality of the interaction between two systems to be certified through local measurements on only one of them. We then develop a novel quantum memory witness, making the approach applicable to gravitationally coupled harmonic oscillators. This witness requires no assumptions about the dynamics, such as Gaussianity. Our results show that the quantumness of gravitational dynamics can be certified with access to only one subsystem, opening the door to asymmetric implementations that can offer conceptual and experimental advantages to probing the quantum nature of the gravitational interaction.

title: Signatures of a Kondo insulator in a multilayer moiré Superlattice
abstractText: Abstract Kondo insulators are paradigmatic strongly correlated materials, traditionally found in f-electron compounds. They originate from the hybridization between itinerant conduction electrons and localized magnetic moments, which opens a gap in the electronic spectrum. Two-dimensional moiré systems provide a new route to flat bands with strong electron correlation, which host localized moments at half filling. Here we report signatures, based on local conductivity measurements using microwave impedance microscopy, of a Kondo insulator in a moiré superlattice of monolayer WS 2 / bilayer WSe 2 , in which one WSe 2 layer carries flat moiré bands and the other dispersive ones. When both layers are partially doped with two holes per moiré unit cell in total, an insulating state appears when the moiré band contains less than one hole. The insulator becomes metallic above a certain threshold magnetic field, evidence for the singlet nature of the Kondo insulator, and the observed behavior is reproduced by a periodic Anderson model. Our results open a route to simulating Kondo physics in tunable moiré systems.

title: Simple eigenvalues and non-vanishing eigenvectors of the Anderson model
abstractText: Abstract We consider the Anderson model on the finite grid $$G = \mathbb {Z}/L_1\mathbb {Z}\times \cdots \times \mathbb {Z}/L_d\mathbb {Z}$$ G = Z / L 1 Z × ⋯ × Z / L d Z , defined by the random Hamiltonian $$H_t=\Delta +tV$$ H t = Δ + t V , where $$\Delta $$ Δ is the discrete Laplacian and $$V=\textrm{diag}(\{\omega _{x}\}_{x\in G})$$ V = diag ( { ω x } x ∈ G ) is a random onsite potential with $$\omega _x\sim \mu $$ ω x ∼ μ i.i.d. We ask the natural question of when $$H_t$$ H t has simple eigenvalues and non-vanishing eigenvectors. We prove that, when $$\mu $$ μ is a continuous probability distribution, $$H_t$$ H t has this property for all but finitely many t values with probability 1. However, when $$\mu $$ μ is a Bernoulli distribution, the conditions fail with positive probability, for which we give a lower bound. We also calculate the exact probability of these conditions being met in the Bernoulli case when $$d = 1$$ d = 1 and $$L = L_1$$ L = L 1 is prime.

title: Symmetry as a common origin of hierarchical emergence and abstraction
abstractText: Many systems of interest exhibit nested emergent layers with their own rules and regularities, and our knowledge about them seems naturally organized around these levels. How do such hierarchical structures arise, and why should observers track these hierarchies so closely? This paper proposes symmetry as an answer to both questions. By combining principles from information theory, group theory, and statistical mechanics, it is shown that dynamical processes that are equivariant with respect to a symmetry group give rise to multiple emergent macroscopic levels arranged according to the algebraic structure of the symmetry. The same symmetries shape the Bayesian beliefs of an observer with only partial access to the system, yielding a matching hierarchy of “abstract” beliefs that can be updated autonomously at different levels of resolution. These ideas are illustrated in Hopfield networks, where familiar macroscopic quantities emerge from known symmetries, and in Boolean models of gene regulation, where symmetries are instead found from the dynamics. The computational advantages provided by symmetry are showcased in Ehrenfest diffusion and epidemic modeling, where abstract beliefs enable Bayesian inference over exponentially large state spaces. These results identify symmetry as a sufficient mechanism for hierarchical emergence and—at the same time—for the capacity of abstract beliefs to mirror the systems they track, making feasible inferential problems that would otherwise be intractable.

title: Heuristic algorithms for the stochastic critical node detection problem
Conformal Holographic Dark Energy and the Neutrino-Mass Tension
abstractText: Recent DESI results suggest a preference for evolving dark energy (DE) over a cosmological constant, motivating the exploration of alternative models for the background expansion. These data also lead to neutrino-mass constraints close to the lower bounds permitted by oscillation experiments. In this work, we propose and test a conformal holographic dark energy (CHDE) model in which the DE density depends on a power law of the conformal time, characterized by an exponent n. The model introduces one additional parameter relative to ΛCDM and reduces to it in the limit n=0. We confront CHDE with BAO, CMB, and SNe Ia datasets, following the combinations used by DESI, and perform parameter inference in both flat and non-flat cosmologies. We find a consistent preference for n≃−0.25 to −0.32, with uncertainties below ±0.1, and disfavor the ΛCDM limit at the 4.4–4.5σ level; however, the model-comparison statistics provide no consistent preference for CHDE over ΛCDM. The resulting neutrino-mass constraints remain compatible with terrestrial limits and yield posterior distributions that peak at positive values, avoiding the negative-mass preference found in ΛCDM. The CHDE model is therefore consistent with current observational constraints and provides a viable alternative to constant dark energy.

Pesticide-exposed bees fail to thermoregulate leading to cold colonies with consequences for offspring development
abstractText: Abstract For many organisms, effective thermoregulation is needed to cope with changing environmental temperatures. But if exposure to pesticides in the environment were to impair this homoeostatic process, reproduction and population viability could be at risk. Focusing on an important insect pollinator, we conducted three complementary experiments exposing bumblebees to a pesticide under different temperature challenges and measuring the impacts on thermoregulatory ability and brood development. First, we reveal that pesticide-exposed individuals (food spiked with a neonicotinoid insecticide) cannot maintain a stable thorax temperature, especially at lower temperatures. Second, that reductions in body temperature are accompanied by behavioural changes with pesticide-exposed colonies failing to maintain the brood temperatures that control bees achieved. Third, that such collective impairment of brood thermoregulation (not the pesticide toxicity to offspring per se) leads to delayed pupal development and reduced adult population growth. Our study provides a plausible mechanistic pathway for why terrestrial insects requiring brood thermoregulation may be vulnerable to decline. With frequent extreme weather events forecasted, our findings have concerning implications for how populations will adequately persist and grow under current pesticide-use regimes with ramifications for pollination services.

title: Loop Quantum Gravity Black Holes Surrounded by Quintessence
abstractText: Quantum gravity corrections act on the near-horizon geometry of a black hole (BH), while dark energy acts on its asymptotic region, and how the two imprints combine is still poorly understood. We study a static, spherically symmetric BH of Loop Quantum Gravity (LQG) surrounded by a quintessence field. The metric function carries the LQG parameters [Formula: see text] and the quintessence parameters [Formula: see text], and for suitable values it has three horizons, a structure found neither in pure LQG BHs nor in classical quintessence BHs. We analyze null and timelike geodesics, photon spheres and the shadow seen by a static observer placed between the event and the cosmological horizons. Sixth-order WKB quasinormal modes (QNMs) of scalar and electromagnetic fields confirm stability over the ranges examined. The quantum term behaves as a short-range repulsive correction: it shrinks the photon sphere and the shadow, raises the QNM oscillation frequency and lowers the light deflection. Quintessence works the other way on the photon sphere, the ringing frequency and the bending. With the Gauss-Bonnet method we obtain a weak deflection angle valid for [Formula: see text], which we check against direct numerical integration, and in which quintessence dominates at large impact parameters and the LQG terms at small ones.

A Study of the Design Space of Motion and Disocclusion Control in Video Generation
abstractText: Abstract Disocclusion occurs when object movement reveals previously hidden content. Existing image‐to‐video methods provide different forms of motion and disocclusion control, yet the design space they span remains poorly understood. In this work, we systematically explore an algorithmic design space spanning motion specification (text‐based versus tracking‐based) and dis‐occlusion specification (text‐based versus image‐based). To facilitate this study, we construct a benchmark consisting of both synthetic scenes and captured scenes, covering rigid and deformable motions, as well as static and dynamic disoccluded objects. We compare existing and adapted methods across this design space to analyze the strengths and limitations of different control strategies for handling disocclusions during motion. Our study reveals that tracking‐based guidance improves motion accuracy, while image‐based guidance improves the fidelity of newly revealed content. However, jointly controlling the appearance and dynamics of disoccluded objects remains a challenging open problem, particularly in scenarios where newly revealed objects undergo their own motion after becoming visible.

title: Guidelines development for design reviews with advanced collaboration tools
abstractText: Abstract Design Reviews (DRs) function as formal governance checkpoints within the product development process where cross-functional stakeholders evaluate design proposals against product requirements to determine their readiness for progression. As design teams become increasingly global, they rely heavily on remote and digital workflows to conduct DRs. While research explores the implementation of new tools to enhance collaboration in DRs, studies often focus on technical feasibility or interaction effects in isolated settings rather than on how these technologies can be embedded in actual industrial processes. In this study, we examine the use of advanced collaboration tools, defined here as digital systems that provide shared spatial environments, in-scene deictic referencing, and independent navigation. Currently, organizations lack actionable guidance on integrating these tools into their DR processes. Thus, this paper develops an evidence-informed set of procedural guidelines for planning, conducting, and documenting DRs using advanced collaboration tools. Working with two automotive companies, we conducted a multi-phase study where two real industrial cases (one per company) were reconstructed to facilitate collaborative workshops aimed at mapping technological capabilities to procedural rules. The analysis draws on established accounts of grounding, workspace awareness, distributed cognition, and organizational routines to interpret the coordination breakdowns observed and the routines that address them. By analyzing verbal data and interaction logs, we developed a set of guidelines grounded in the specific coordination problems identified by practitioners and the technological capabilities required to resolve them. The resulting guidelines identify five domains, including pre-read and preparation, attention management, documentation and traceability, integration and handoff, and modality and role distribution. The guidelines provide a transferable structure for organizations to transform advanced collaboration tools from isolated visualizers into reliable, managed elements of the DRs workflow.

abstractText: We prove the stability under lamination of a set of real, symmetric 3 times × $\times$ 3 matrices that can be interpreted as a subset of the effective conductivities of a polycrystal made by a single, arbitrarily fixed basic crystal. Constructed in the companion paper [1], such a set constitutes a two-dimensional portion of the boundary of the pertinent upper G G $G$ -closure because it corresponds to materials saturating a well-known polyconvex lower bound; we prove that laminations between any two points of such a set still belong to the set.

title: Depth-enhanced molecular imaging with two-photon oblique plane microscopy
abstractText: Abstract High-numerical-aperture (NA) oblique plane microscopy enables noninvasive fluorescence imaging of subcellular dynamics without radical sample modification. However, performance degrades at depth in multicellular specimens as scattering and refractive-index heterogeneity raise out-of-focus background. We report a two-photon oblique plane microscope that improves resolution at depth by combining high-NA single-objective detection with multiphoton plane illumination. The microscope achieves ~ 300 nm lateral and ~ 650 nm axial resolution, with single-molecule sensitivity and < 60 nm localization precision in vivo. Compared with two-photon point scanning, the lower illumination NA delivers order-of-magnitude lower peak intensity, enabling > 5 × faster volumetric acquisition (up to 3.25 × 10 6 voxels s −1 ). In multicellular contexts, near-infrared nonlinear excitation enhances contrast throughout the illumination depth by ~ 2 × and restores volumetric resolving power by > 2 × relative to linear excitation. We demonstrate these capabilities through molecular imaging of epithelial tissue, stem-cell-derived gastruloids, and living fruit fly embryos, including multicolor transcription-factor dynamics, optogenetic subcellular control, and single-mRNA tracking, all using standard glass-based mounting.

title: Heterogeneity in carbon emission efficiency across global marine capture fisheries: a metafrontier analysis of technology gaps and reduction potentials
abstractText: Improving the carbon emission efficiency of marine capture fisheries is important for the sustainable development of fisheries under climate change. Using 66 major marine fishing countries over 1995–2017 as the sample, we divided the countries into three groups by fishing structure: high-input predatory fish-dominated, mixed, and small pelagic and other finfish-dominated. We measured carbon emission efficiency with a slacks-based measure (SBM) model with undesirable outputs and a metafrontier approach, and decomposed the potential emission reduction into managerial inefficiency and the technology gap. The results show the following. (1) Carbon emission efficiency was generally low, with a mean metafrontier efficiency of 0.331, and the differences between groups were closely related to catch value. (2) The technology gap was concentrated in the high-input predatory fish-dominated group and the small pelagic and other finfish-dominated group, and its causes differed across countries: in Vietnam, Thailand and Malaysia it was associated with fuel-intensive fishing operations, whereas in Peru and Chile it stemmed from the low value of the catch. (3) The mean annual potential carbon emission reduction of the sample countries was 85.4 Mt CO 2 -eq, about 53% of their total emissions, and was concentrated in countries such as Indonesia, India and Vietnam. (4) Managerial inefficiency was the main source of the reduction potential, accounting for 69%. In the mixed group, almost all of the potential came from managerial inefficiency; in the high-input predatory fish-dominated group, the technology gap dominated; and in the small pelagic and other finfish-dominated group, both sources contributed. Countries should therefore choose different pathways according to the source of their reduction potential. For most countries, catching up with the best practice of similar countries could release most of the potential with existing technology, especially in countries where the potential is concentrated, such as Indonesia and India. Countries whose technology gap is accompanied by high fuel intensity should focus on promoting energy-saving fishing gear and propulsion technology, while countries that mainly land low-value catch should increase the value of their catch.

title: Supporting Families of Children With Cancer Using a Virtual Assistant for Social Care: Development and Usability Study
abstractText: Abstract Background Families of children with cancer face substantial financial, social, and emotional stressors, including unmet health-related social needs (HRSN) and toxic stress, which contribute to disparities. Virtual assistants (VAs) offer a scalable option to screen for HRSN and connect families to resources, but their design and acceptability in pediatric oncology are not well characterized. Objective The objective of this study was to evaluate a VA prototype designed to screen for HRSN and reduce toxic stress among families of children with cancer. Methods A 2-phase mixed methods study was conducted to co-design and evaluate a VA prototype for caregivers of children with cancer. In phase 1, a community advisory board (CAB) including health care providers and a parent advocate (n=8) iteratively refined VA content, tone, and interface through 3 virtual co-design sessions. In phase 2, caregivers (n=40) completed in-person VA prototype usability sessions that included structured observation, a semistructured interview, the System Usability Scale (SUS), a caregiver satisfaction survey, and a reaction card task. Social drivers of health, rurality, and neighborhood disadvantage were characterized using survey data and geocoded indices. Results CAB feedback refined prototype components including community resources, stress management, conversation history, and resource feedback. In phase 2, usability was high (SUS mean 82.6, SD 14.0); 95% (38/40) of caregivers rated the VA as easy to use and good to use, and 92.5% (37/40) reported that the VA motivated them to remain engaged during screening and resource identification. Qualitative analysis revealed that caregivers favored the VA’s simplicity and its potential to provide timely support, particularly shortly after diagnosis. Participants expressed strong preferences for electronic health record integration to streamline care, though they noted concerns regarding privacy and “app fatigue” as potential adoption barriers. Reaction card responses were predominantly positive (eg, “accessible,” “easy,” and “useful”). Greater socioeconomic vulnerability was associated with higher usability ratings, while rural and medically underserved caregivers reported lower confidence and more negative desirability attributes. Conclusions The stakeholder-informed VA to address HRSN and toxic stress in pediatric oncology was highly usable and acceptable in prototype testing. Future work should evaluate live deployment, resource linkage, toxic stress outcomes, and equity in larger, more diverse, and longitudinal studies.
